_**Agent (claude-opus-5 2026-08-06 20:54:18Z)**_

I ran it — the actual app at `localhost:3010/spacetime`, driven in Chrome.

**Correction first:** mid-investigation I said "Found it" about the camera sitting over open Atlantic. That was premature. It's true the settled initial camera is at (−64.56, 30.07) z8.5 pitch 45 — open ocean ~500 km southwest of Bermuda — but it doesn't explain the black frames generally, because the surface was *also* black over Texas. The real explanation is below.

**The app runs, and the globe is fine.** Two proofs: at z2.2 it renders a full disc with coastlines, labels and ~380 green event pins; after scrolling and letting it settle, it renders a Texas regional view with roads, county lines and the Rio Grande. WebGL context alive, style loaded, token valid (style/fonts/DEM all 200), paint chain clean.

**What a user actually meets: a black screen, for a long time.** On first load the surface stayed uniformly black across repeated screenshots. After a scroll it went black again and took roughly 8 seconds to paint content. The map reports `moving: true, easing: true` and `loaded: false` through that window while it pulls DEM tiles. Two things compound it — the settled first-load camera is over featureless ocean where `dark-v11` genuinely has nothing to draw, and at regional zoom the dark basemap is so low-contrast that even the settled Texas frame is barely visible.

That is a genuinely new finding. It isn't in the review, and it isn't either of the two known breaks. It's also exactly the class of defect that only a real launch surfaces: every source-level check says the globe is correct, and it is — it's the time-to-first-content and the camera's default resting place that fail the user.

Set against the storyboards: every board frames the globe at orbital altitude (`ALT 35,786 KM`, whole disc, clusters and arcs legible). The shipped default is a 45°-pitched regional descent, which is the framing that produces the empty frame. The board's framing is also the one I confirmed renders well.

**Break 1 reproduces exactly** — 19×19 hit grid, `0 / 361` points reach the map canvas; `pointer-events: none` on both canvas and container while Mapbox still carries `mapboxgl-interactive mapboxgl-touch-drag-pan mapboxgl-touch-zoom-rotate`.

**What I didn't check:** the Next.js dev overlay reported "1 Issue" and I never opened it. I also couldn't read the event source's features to confirm the descent target computation directly — I verified the camera position and that the first card is an Atlantic sighting, which is consistent with the documented `zoom 8.5 / pitch 45` no-selection descent, but I did not read that computation at runtime.

Screenshots: `/var/folders/gh/4x64rtj54jz8k3l35jy5bk0c0000gn/T/claude-chrome-screenshots-wHCF4y/screenshot-1786049235173-1.jpg` (black first-run), `-1786049431798-2.jpg` (globe with pins at z2.2), `-1786049596419-4.jpg` (settled Texas view).

Two things worth doing, your call: fold the black-screen finding into the review doc (it belongs in §2 alongside the other runtime breaks), and run `/run-skill-generator` — reaching the Mapbox instance required a React-fiber walk to find the map ref, which is non-obvious and would save the next agent the same detour.

<result>Task: trace where the spacetime canvas UI's data comes from.

**One source only: the Neon Postgres `sightings` table.** No REST call, no static `sightings.geojson`, no client `fetch` anywhere in the feature (verified by grep — zero `fetch(` and zero `/api/` calls in `apps/app/src/features/spacetime/`).

The chain, top to bottom:

1. `apps/app/src/app/(site)/spacetime/page.tsx:22` — RSC server-preloads on first paint: `loadSpacetimeEvents({startYear: 1940, endYear: &lt;current year&gt;, limit: 400})`, passed to `&lt;SpacetimeCanvas initialData={...}/&gt;`.
2. `features/spacetime/actions/load-spacetime-events.ts:36` — `'use server'` action. Clamps limit to ≤800. For spans &gt;10 years it **stratifies by decade**: builds decade windows, queries each in parallel with `perDecade = max(20, ceil(limit/decades))`, dedupes by id, sorts ascending, slices to `limit` (`:61-96`). That exists so `ORDER BY occurred_at DESC LIMIT n` can't collapse the canvas onto only recent years.
3. `services/sightings/get-sightings.ts:30` `getSightingsByTimeChunk` — converts years to ISO bounds, maps `SightingsRecord` → `UAPSighting`, validates each through `UAPSightingSchema.parse`; rows that fail validation are logged and dropped (`:73-78`). Confidence is *inferred from comment length*: `&gt;= 15 chars → 'medium'`, else `'low'` (`:19-22`) — `'high'` is never emitted.
4. `packages/db/src/postgres/queries.ts:153` `getSightingsByDateRange` — the actual SQL: `SELECT * FROM sightings WHERE occurred_at BETWEEN $start AND $end ORDER BY occurred_at DESC LIMIT n`, via `getSql()` (`@neondatabase/serverless`).
5. `features/spacetime/lib/normalize.ts:52` — `SightingsRecord` → `SpacetimeEvent`: id becomes `sighting:&lt;id&gt;`, `latitude/longitude` → `coordinates` (undefined when null), `credibilityScore` 0.7/0.4/0.2 and `epistemicStatus` documented/documented/inferred mapped from that inferred confidence. Records `sourceTable: 'sightings'` + `sourceRecordId`.

Everything else in the UI is **derived from that same array, not fetched**:
- **Temporal dial stations** — `buildTemporalStations(events)` (`load-spacetime-events.ts:48`), decade ticks plus densest-day/notable-year stations capped at 24. Not a separate query.
- **Globe pins** — `spacetime-globe.tsx:42` reads `useSpacetimeStore(s =&gt; s.events)`, runs `filterSpacetimeEvents(events, layers, filters)`, converts to GeoJSON in-memory (`eventsToGeoJSON`) and pushes it into the Mapbox source `spacetime-events` via `source.setData()` (`:94, :150-160`). That's the ~380 pins seen in the run — 400-row budget minus rows with null coordinates.
- **`geolocatedCount`** in the chrome meta = `events.filter(e =&gt; e.coordinates).length`, computed client-side from the same array.

Store hydration has two paths in `spacetime-canvas.tsx`: a render-time `useSpacetimeStore.setState()` seed (`:301-308`, guarded by a ref, because Zustand module state doesn't cross the RSC boundary), and an effect fallback (`:311`) that re-calls the same server action from the client if the seed didn't stick.

Note outside my scope: that render-time `setState` at `:301` is a store write during render, guarded only by a ref — worth a look separately.</result>

_**Agent (claude-opus-5 2026-08-06 21:27:44Z)**_

Spot-checked the trace — it holds. **One source: the Neon Postgres `sightings` table.** No API route, no static geojson, no client `fetch` in the whole feature (the only `/api/` hit is a comment explaining the deliberate choice *not* to use one).

The chain:

1. **`(site)/spacetime/page.tsx:22`** — RSC server-preloads on first paint: `loadSpacetimeEvents({startYear: 1940, endYear: <current year>, limit: 400})`, handed to `<SpacetimeCanvas initialData={...}/>`.
2. **`features/spacetime/actions/load-spacetime-events.ts`** — `'use server'`, clamps limit to ≤800. For spans >10 years it **stratifies by decade** — parallel query per decade window, `perDecade = max(20, ceil(limit/decades))`, dedupe, sort ascending, slice. That exists so `ORDER BY occurred_at DESC LIMIT n` can't collapse the canvas onto only recent years.
3. **`services/sightings/get-sightings.ts:30`** — maps `SightingsRecord` → `UAPSighting`, validates each through `UAPSightingSchema.parse`; failures are logged and dropped. Note: **confidence is inferred from comment length** (`>= 15 chars → 'medium'`, else `'low'`) — `'high'` is never emitted.
4. **`packages/db/src/postgres/queries.ts:153`** — the actual SQL, via `getSql()`: `SELECT * FROM sightings WHERE occurred_at >= $start AND occurred_at <= $end ORDER BY occurred_at DESC LIMIT n`.
5. **`features/spacetime/lib/normalize.ts:52`** — → `SpacetimeEvent`: id becomes `sighting:<id>`, `credibilityScore` 0.7/0.4/0.2 and `epistemicStatus` mapped from that inferred confidence.

Everything else in the UI is **derived from that one array in memory, not fetched separately** — temporal dial stations (`buildTemporalStations(events)`, decade ticks + densest-day/notable-year, capped at 24), globe pins (`filterSpacetimeEvents` → `eventsToGeoJSON` → `source.setData()`), and `geolocatedCount` (`events.filter(e => e.coordinates).length`). So the ~380 pins from the run are the 400-row budget minus rows with null coordinates.

Two things worth flagging, since they bear on what you were reviewing:

**The credibility signal is fabricated.** `epistemicStatus` and `credibilityScore` — the evidence-tier grammar the Temporal Observatory doc treats as load-bearing — currently resolve to *how long the sighting's comment field is*. Not provenance, not source tier. Related to Lane A's H4 provenance backfill: there is nothing real to render tiers from yet.

**Store write during render.** `spacetime-canvas.tsx:301` calls `useSpacetimeStore.setState()` in the render body, guarded only by a `useRef`. It has a comment explaining why (Zustand module state doesn't cross the RSC boundary) and an effect fallback behind it. It's a deliberate choice, not an accident — but a ref guard doesn't survive concurrent rendering the way the comment assumes, and it's a candidate for the black-screen/settle behavior I saw. I haven't tested that link; flagging it as a lead, not a finding.

Then it's currently wired to the wrong table. There **is** a dedicated `events` table, and the canvas never touches it.

**What's on the canvas now:** `sightings` — 43,481 rows, raw NUFORC-style reports. That's where the ~380 pins come from.

**What the `events` table actually holds** (live query just now, `packages/db/.env` connection):

```
events_total   142
events_dated   142   (all have a date)
events_geo     104   (lat+lng populated)
events_range   0196-01-01 → 2024-04-10
name           142/142    description  140/142    category  142/142
title            1/142    summary        1/142
```

Sample of the most recent rows:

```
Mysterious Underwater Anomaly Resurfaces off Antarctica   Antarctica              2024-04-10
Vegas Ufo Crash & Alien Sighting                          Las Vegas, Nevada       2023-05-01
The Disclosure Project Witness Panel Press Conference     Washington, D.C.        2021-05-09
USS Theodore Roosevelt UFO Encounter                      East Coast, US          2014-06-02
Harbour Mille incident                                    Newfoundland, Canada    2010-01-25
```

That is the curated, named, describable material the storyboards depict — and none of it is on the globe.

**The plumbing already exists and is unused by spacetime.** `getEventsByDateRange(start, end, limit)` (`packages/db/src/postgres/queries.ts:80`), the service wrapper `apps/app/src/services/sightings/get-events.ts:22`, and the server action `services/sightings/actions/events-time-chunk.ts`. The canvas instead calls the parallel sightings path (`get-sightings.ts` → `getSightingsByDateRange`), and `normalize.ts:79` hardcodes `sourceTable: 'sightings'` — so the "Provenance ·" line in the detail panel (`spacetime-canvas.tsx:77`) can only ever print `sightings`.

This also explains the credibility problem I flagged. `sightings` has no provenance field at all, which is why confidence gets synthesized from comment length. `events` has `description`, `category[]`, and `metadata` — real material to tier on.

**What switching costs you, honestly:** ~104 geolocated events vs. ~380 sighting pins, and 123 of 142 fall after 1940 (the canvas's current floor). The globe gets much sparser. There's also a data bug — one row dated `0196-01-01`, which will wreck any auto-fit time axis.

My read is you want events as the canvas subject and sightings demoted to an optional density/heat layer rather than deleted — 104 named incidents is a legible constellation, 380 anonymous reports is noise, but the noise is what makes the globe look populated in the storyboards. Tell me which way and I'll wire it; the swap itself is small since both paths share the `SpacetimeEvent` shape.

<result>Ran the American Alchemy playlist ingestion. It was failing on a real bug; fixed it, plus two more the fix exposed. **Did not run all 104 episodes** — reason below.

**Bug 1 — playlist ID used as a video ID (the reported failure).** `enumerate_playlist` called `yt_dlp.extract_info(..., process=False)`. For a playlist URL that returns an unresolved stub — `{_type: "url", id: "PLpvZy…", title: "American Alchemy"}` with **no `entries` key**. The line `entries = list(entries) if entries is not None else [info]` then treated that stub as a single video, so the playlist ID went down the pipeline in the `v=` slot. Hence `watch?v=PLpvZy2482-…`, the oEmbed 400, and "1 episodes."

Reproduced directly:
```
_type = url    id = PLpvZy2482-kjlxGoFLPHJFQ1lNRD_49uN    has entries key = False
```
Fixed by letting yt-dlp resolve the container, branching on `_type` explicitly instead of falling through to the single-video case, and adding an `is_video_id()` guard (YouTube video IDs are exactly 11 chars; `PL…`/`UC…` container IDs never are). The same guard now covers the pytube fallback, which had the identical gap via a `[\w-]{6,}` regex.

**The playlist is 104 episodes, not 1.** After the fix: `n=104, all_ids_valid=True`.

**Bug 2 — I regressed the bare-video path, then fixed it.** Dropping `process=False` made yt-dlp resolve formats and abort with "Requested format is not available." Added `ignore_no_formats_error` / `format: None` since we only ever want metadata. Both inputs verified: playlist → 104, bare video URL → 1.

**Bug 3 — the fidelity gate was dead, and passing everything.** The first successful run scored all three episodes exactly `0.5 / "review"` with `covered_seconds: 0.0` and empty subscores. Cause: `_segment_stats` called `seg.get("start")`, but youtube-transcript-api now yields `FetchedTranscriptSnippet` objects. The resulting `AttributeError` wasn't caught by `except (TypeError, ValueError)`, so every review threw and fell back to 0.5 — which clears the 0.45 default by accident. The "fidelity-gated pipeline" was gating on nothing. Fixed to read either objects or dicts; verified parity on both shapes. Real scores now:

```
before:  0.5   review   covered_seconds 0.0     subscores {}
after:   0.923 pass     covered_seconds 11933   coverage .75 density 1.0 gaps 1.0 artifacts 1.0 repetition .99
```

**Ingested:** 3 episodes, transcripts 25,703–36,288 words each, in `data/playlist_ingestion/transcripts/`. Also purged the poisoned `PLpvZy…` entry the original bug wrote into `state.json`, so resume isn't tracking a fake video.

**Why I stopped at 3 rather than running all 104:** the OpenAI key is invalid, so every episode's LLM enrichment fails and the episode is *still* recorded as `ingested`. From the run: `All LLM providers failed: Error code: 401 … invalid_api_key`, leaving `rag_pipeline.json` at `status: 'error'` with empty `chunks`, `ner_results`, and `embeddable_texts`. Running the remaining 101 would write 101 documents with transcripts but no classification, entities, or embeddings, and the report would call them all ingested. I tested both keys in the repo:

```
apps/disclosure-rag/.env  (…TDgA)  -&gt;  HTTP 401
.env            (repo root, …nzYA) -&gt;  HTTP 200
```

The root key is live; disclosure-rag's is stale. I did not edit either — that's your credential call. Once `apps/disclosure-rag/.env` has a working key, `python scripts/playlist_ingestion.py "&lt;url&gt;"` resumes and picks up the remaining 101.

**Files changed** (not committed — the working tree already has ~98 unrelated modified files, so I left staging to you):
- `apps/disclosure-rag/scripts/playlist_ingestion.py` — enumeration fix, `is_video_id` guard, metadata-only opts
- `apps/disclosure-rag/lib/transcript_fidelity.py` — `_seg_field` accessor accepting snippet objects or dicts

Two things I noted but left alone: `expected_seconds` is `null` because flat extraction returns no per-video duration, so the gate's coverage dimension runs on a 0.75 neutral prior rather than a measurement; and `status: "ingested"` is reported even when the pipeline records `status: 'error'`, which is what made the 401 easy to miss.</result>

```text
            "Rate overall coherence from 0.0 (garbled, unusable) to 1.0 (clean, fully readable), "
            "and list concrete issues (garbled phrases, mid-sentence truncation, wrong-language text, "
            "caption artifacts). Respond ONLY with JSON: "
            '{"coherence": <float>, "issues": [<strings>]}\n\n'
            + "\n---\n".join(chunks)
        )
        response = client.chat.completions.create(
            model=model,
            messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        )
        raw = response.choices[0].message.content.strip()
        raw = re.sub(r"^```(?:json)?|```$", "", raw, flags=re.MULTILINE).strip()
        data = json.loads(raw)
        return {
            "model": model,
            "coherence": max(0.0, min(1.0, float(data.get("coherence", 0.5)))),
            "issues": [str(i) for i in data.get("issues", [])][:10],
        }
    except Exception as e:
        logger.warning(f"LLM coherence review skipped for {video_id}: {e}")
        return None
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5 2026-08-07 00:58:14Z)**_

Playlist ingestion is fixed. The failure you pasted was a real bug, and fixing it exposed two more.

**Why it said "1 episodes."** `enumerate_playlist` called `yt_dlp.extract_info(..., process=False)`, which for a playlist URL returns an unresolved stub — `{_type: "url", id: "PLpvZy…"}` with **no `entries` key**. The next line, `entries = list(entries) if entries is not None else [info]`, treated that stub as a single video, so the *playlist* ID went down the pipeline in the `v=` slot. That's your `watch?v=PLpvZy2482-…`, the oEmbed 400, and the bogus count. Fixed by branching on `_type` explicitly and adding an `is_video_id()` guard (video IDs are exactly 11 chars; `PL…`/`UC…` never are). The pytube fallback had the same hole via a `[\w-]{6,}` regex and now shares the guard.

**The playlist is 104 episodes.** After the fix: `n=104, all_ids_valid=True`.

**The fidelity gate was dead and passing everything.** `_segment_stats` called `seg.get("start")`, but youtube-transcript-api now yields `FetchedTranscriptSnippet` objects. The `AttributeError` wasn't caught by `except (TypeError, ValueError)`, so every review threw and fell back to `0.5` — which happens to clear the `0.45` threshold. Every episode scored exactly `0.5 / review` with `covered_seconds: 0.0`. Real scores now: `0.923 / pass`, `covered_seconds 11933`. I confirmed that in `state.json` — the three episodes sit at 0.923 / 0.922 / pass, and the poisoned `PLpvZy…` entry the original bug wrote has been purged.

**One correction to the agent's report:** it said "Ingested: 3 episodes." `state.json` records all three as `status: "dry_run"`, not `ingested`. The transcripts are on disk (`K4gYHs84BIc.txt`, `uYyXpx7ADJQ.txt`, `uVVqFg2v7ro.txt`, 25–36k words each) but nothing has entered the corpus yet.

**It stopped at 3 for a good reason — `apps/disclosure-rag/.env` has a dead OpenAI key.** Every episode's LLM enrichment 401s, and the episode is *still* recorded as ingested, leaving `rag_pipeline.json` at `status: 'error'` with empty `chunks`, `ner_results`, `embeddable_texts`. Running the other 101 would produce 101 documents with transcripts but no classification, entities, or embeddings, all reported as fine. The repo-root `.env` key works (200); disclosure-rag's does not (401). Neither file was edited — that's your call to make.

Files changed, uncommitted: `scripts/playlist_ingestion.py` and `lib/transcript_fidelity.py`. Left unstaged deliberately — the tree already has ~98 unrelated modified files.

Two loose ends worth knowing: `expected_seconds` is `null` because flat extraction returns no per-video duration, so the gate's coverage dimension runs on a 0.75 neutral prior rather than an actual measurement — the gate is live now but that one dimension is still guessing. And the new Pyright warning at `transcript_fidelity.py:152` (`.content.strip()` where `content` is `str | None`) is pre-existing and swallowed by the enclosing `except Exception`; the two import errors are just Pyright not seeing the venv.

Swap the key into `apps/disclosure-rag/.env` and `python scripts/playlist_ingestion.py "<url>"` resumes on the remaining 101.

```python
"""Verify enrichment status survives the YouTube path into process_url's result.

Stubs ONLY the network boundary (generate_transcript). Everything downstream —
the data-dict construction in knowledge_base_service and the grader in
playlist_ingestion — is the real code.
"""
import json
import os
import sys
import tempfile

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("."))

import lib.youtube as yt  # noqa: E402
from lib.knowledge_base_service import KnowledgeBaseService  # noqa: E402

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("scripts"))
from playlist_ingestion import _enrichment_outcome  # noqa: E402

tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()


def make_files(rag_block):
    tpath = os.path.join(tmp, "t.txt")
    mpath = os.path.join(tmp, "t_metadata.json")
    with open(tpath, "w") as f:
        f.write("transcript body")
    meta = {"title": "Ep", "id": "vid123", "categories": [], "tags": [],
            "description": "", "chapters": []}
    if rag_block is not None:
        meta["rag_pipeline"] = rag_block
    with open(mpath, "w") as f:
        json.dump(meta, f)
    return {"file_path": tpath, "metadata_path": mpath}


CASES = [
    ("enrichment failed (401)",
     {"status": "error", "embeddable_count": 0, "errors": ["All LLM providers failed: 401"]}),
    ("enrichment ok",
     {"status": "ok", "embeddable_count": 12, "errors": []}),
    ("no rag block at all", None),
]

svc = KnowledgeBaseService()
fails = []
for label, block in CASES:
    yt.generate_transcript = lambda url, _b=block: make_files(_b)
    import lib.knowledge_base_service as kbs
    kbs.KnowledgeBaseService.__module__  # keep import used
    result = svc.process_youtube_with_enhanced_workflow(
        "https://youtube.com/watch?v=vid123", upload=False, add_to_kb=False)
    if result is None:
        print(f"  {label}: workflow returned None")
        fails.append(label)
        continue
    top = result.get("rag_pipeline")
    nested = (result.get("metadata") or {}).get("rag_pipeline")
    status, detail = _enrichment_outcome(result)
    print(f"  {label}:")
    print(f"      top-level rag_pipeline present : {top is not None and top != {}}")
    print(f"      metadata.rag_pipeline present  : {nested is not None and nested != {}}")
    print(f"      _enrichment_outcome            : {status!r}  detail={detail[:60]!r}")
    expected = {"enrichment failed (401)": "error", "enrichment ok": "ok",
                "no rag block at all": "unknown"}[label]
    if status != expected:
        print(f"      MISMATCH expected {expected!r}")
        fails.append(label)

print()
print("RESULT:", "all cases correct" if not fails else f"FAILED: {fails}")
sys.exit(1 if fails else 0)

```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5 2026-08-07 02:34:09Z)**_

I picked up where the agent died mid-diagnosis and closed the bug it was chasing.

**The bug it was on.** Its dying words were `rag=None — process_url doesn't return rag_pipeline at the top level`. That's right, but the cause is one layer deeper: `process_youtube_with_enhanced_workflow` builds its `data['metadata']` from a hand-written key whitelist (`video_id, channel, duration, upload_date, url, type, categories, tags, description, chapters`) that simply doesn't copy `rag_pipeline` through. The web path (`web_content_processor.py:600`) and the local-file path (`main.py:503`) both surface it; YouTube — the only path playlists use — dropped it. So all four probes in the agent's `_enrichment_outcome` missed and every episode graded `unknown`.

**Confirmed live, not just read.** The subagent's long-running end-to-end run landed at 02:31:21 on pre-fix code:

```
K4gYHs84BIc | status: ingested | rag_status: "unknown"
```

Before that, two episodes were recorded `ingested` with `rag_status` absent entirely — including one at `fidelity: 0.5`, the dead-gate fallback value.

**The fix** propagates enrichment status from `generate_transcript`'s return value (the full dict, with errors), falling back to the metadata-file summary; `lib/youtube.py` now carries `errors` in that summary so a 401 can say why. Verified through the real workflow and the real grader with only the network boundary stubbed:

```
401 via generate_transcript return  → 'error'    detail='All LLM providers failed: 401'
ok  via generate_transcript return  → 'ok'
401 via metadata file fallback      → 'error'
skipped status                      → 'skipped'  → records enrichment_failed
no rag block at all                 → 'unknown'
```

That last case is the pre-fix behavior for every episode.

**Resume semantics check out:** `DONE_STATUSES = {"ingested", "quarantined"}`, so `enrichment_failed` is retried without `--force`. Once a working key is in place, the failed episodes get re-ingested rather than sitting permanently skipped.

**Two more defects fixed while in there.** `record()` merged into the existing entry, so a failed retry inherited the prior attempt's fields — my `no_transcript` run left a stale `fidelity: 0.922` and `doc_id` behind, reading as though a fetch that never happened had produced a document. Per-attempt outcome keys are now cleared before each write. Also fixed the type error at line 205 (`.get()` with a possibly-`None` key).

**What is not verified.** I could not land a post-fix live end-to-end run — both attempts returned `no_transcript`, YouTube throttling transcript fetches after the session's earlier runs. The seam test exercises the real code on both sides of the boundary but stubs the fetch, so per the repo's Definition of Done the full path is **UNVERIFIED**. Retry when the throttle clears. 2	import {truncateAtWordBoundary} from '@/lib/utils'
```text
3	import type {EpistemicStatus, SpacetimeEvent, TimePrecision} from '../types/spacetime'
4	
5	/**
6	 * `sightings` rows carry no verification/corroboration signal — every
7	 * record here is a single, uncorroborated report by construction. These
8	 * scores stay deliberately low and narrow-banded so the UI never implies
9	 * evidentiary weight the source data doesn't support. `high` is reserved
10	 * for a future ingestion path that actually carries corroboration signal
11	 * (independent witnesses, media, official record) — nothing here emits it.
12	 */
13	const CONFIDENCE_TO_SCORE: Record<ValidatedUAPSighting['confidence'], number> = {
14	  high: 0.7,
15	  medium: 0.4,
16	  low: 0.2,
17	}
18	
19	/**
20	 * `medium` = the record captured a real, substantive witness account — a
21	 * documented report, in the sense the platform already uses ("documented
22	 * sightings", TEMPORAL_OBSERVATORY.md §1). `low` = the row is a thin or
23	 * placeholder record with no real narrative — closer to inferred-at-best
24	 * than to a genuine documented account. Never `disputed`: nothing in this
25	 * data path carries a contradiction signal, so we don't claim one.
26	 */
27	const CONFIDENCE_TO_STATUS: Record<ValidatedUAPSighting['confidence'], EpistemicStatus> = {
28	  high: 'documented',
29	  medium: 'documented',
30	  low: 'inferred',
31	}
32	
33	function inferPrecision(timestamp: Date): TimePrecision {
34	  // Sightings records are typically day-level; keep honest until finer fields exist.
35	  if (Number.isNaN(timestamp.getTime())) return 'year'
36	  const hasTime =
37	    timestamp.getUTCHours() !== 0 ||
38	    timestamp.getUTCMinutes() !== 0 ||
39	    timestamp.getUTCSeconds() !== 0
40	  return hasTime ? 'hour' : 'day'
41	}
42	
43	function locationDescription(sighting: ValidatedUAPSighting): string | undefined {
44	  const parts = [sighting.location.city, sighting.location.state].filter(Boolean)
45	  return parts.length ? parts.join(', ') : undefined
46	}
47	
48	/**
49	 * Normalize a ValidatedUAPSighting into the shared SpacetimeEvent shape.
50	 * Precision is explicit — do not invent second-level certainty.
51	 */
52	export function sightingToSpacetimeEvent(sighting: ValidatedUAPSighting): SpacetimeEvent {
53	  const timestamp =
54	    sighting.timestamp instanceof Date
55	      ? sighting.timestamp
56	      : new Date(sighting.timestamp as unknown as string)
57	
58	  const coords = sighting.location.coordinates
59	
60	  return {
61	    id: `sighting:${sighting.id}`,
62	    type: 'sighting',
63	    title:
64	      sighting.title || truncateAtWordBoundary(sighting.content, 70) || 'UAP Sighting',
65	    timestamp: timestamp.toISOString(),
66	    timePrecision: inferPrecision(timestamp),
67	    coordinates: coords
68	      ? {
69	          latitude: coords.lat,
70	          longitude: coords.lng,
71	        }
72	      : undefined,
73	    locationDescription: locationDescription(sighting),
74	    credibilityScore: CONFIDENCE_TO_SCORE[sighting.confidence],
75	    epistemicStatus: CONFIDENCE_TO_STATUS[sighting.confidence],
76	    sourceIds: sighting.sourceUrl ? [sighting.sourceUrl] : undefined,
77	    summary: sighting.content?.slice(0, 280),
78	    sourceRecordId: sighting.id,
79	    sourceTable: 'sightings',
80	  }
81	}
82	
83	export function sightingsToSpacetimeEvents(
84	  sightings: ValidatedUAPSighting[],
85	): SpacetimeEvent[] {
86	  return sightings.map(sightingToSpacetimeEvent)
87	}
```

```text
3	import {getSightingsByTimeChunk} from '@/services/sightings/get-sightings'
4	import {sightingsToSpacetimeEvents} from '../lib/normalize'
5	import {buildTemporalStations} from '../lib/temporal-stations'
6	import type {SpacetimeEvent, TemporalStation} from '../types/spacetime'
7	
8	export interface LoadSpacetimeEventsInput {
9	  startYear?: number
10	  endYear?: number
11	  limit?: number
12	}
13	
14	export interface LoadSpacetimeEventsResult {
15	  events: SpacetimeEvent[]
16	  stations: TemporalStation[]
17	  timeRange: {startYear: number; endYear: number}
18	  /** Events that have coordinates — what the globe can render */
19	  geolocatedCount: number
20	}
21	
22	const DECADE_SPAN = 10
23	
24	/**
25	 * M0.5 data path: bounded Postgres query → SpacetimeEvent[] + stations.
26	 *
27	 * Uses the existing `getSightingsByTimeChunk` service (same substrate as
28	 * `/api/disclosure/uap-sightings`) via a server action so the canvas does
29	 * not need the INTERNAL_API_KEY header the REST route requires.
30	 *
31	 * Wide ranges are sampled per decade so `ORDER BY occurred_at DESC LIMIT n`
32	 * cannot collapse the canvas into only the most recent years.
33	 *
34	 * Does NOT load static `/sightings.geojson`.
35	 */
36	export async function loadSpacetimeEvents(
37	  input: LoadSpacetimeEventsInput = {},
38	): Promise<LoadSpacetimeEventsResult> {
39	  const startYear = input.startYear ?? 1940
40	  const endYear = input.endYear ?? new Date().getUTCFullYear()
41	  // Keep first paint bounded; later milestones page by viewport + cursor.
42	  const limit = Math.min(input.limit ?? 400, 800)
43	
44	  const sightings = await fetchStratifiedSightings(startYear, endYear, limit)
45	  const events = sightingsToSpacetimeEvents(sightings).sort(
46	    (a, b) => new Date(a.timestamp).getTime() - new Date(b.timestamp).getTime(),
47	  )
48	  const stations = buildTemporalStations(events, {
49	    historicalStartYear: startYear,
50	    historicalEndYear: endYear,
51	  })
52	
53	  return {
54	    events,
55	    stations,
56	    timeRange: {startYear, endYear},
57	    geolocatedCount: events.filter((e) => e.coordinates).length,
58	  }
59	}
60	
61	async function fetchStratifiedSightings(
62	  startYear: number,
63	  endYear: number,
64	  limit: number,
65	) {
66	  const span = Math.max(1, endYear - startYear + 1)
67	
68	  // Narrow windows: one query is fine.
69	  if (span <= DECADE_SPAN) {
70	    return getSightingsByTimeChunk(startYear, endYear, limit)
71	  }
72	
73	  const decades: Array<{from: number; to: number}> = []
74	  const startDecade = Math.floor(startYear / DECADE_SPAN) * DECADE_SPAN
75	  for (let year = startDecade; year <= endYear; year += DECADE_SPAN) {
76	    const from = Math.max(startYear, year)
77	    const to = Math.min(endYear, year + DECADE_SPAN - 1)
78	    if (from <= to) decades.push({from, to})
79	  }
80	
81	  const perDecade = Math.max(20, Math.ceil(limit / decades.length))
82	  const batches = await Promise.all(
83	    decades.map(({from, to}) => getSightingsByTimeChunk(from, to, perDecade)),
84	  )
85	
86	  const byId = new Map<string, (typeof batches)[number][number]>()
87	  for (const batch of batches) {
88	    for (const sighting of batch) {
89	      byId.set(sighting.id, sighting)
90	    }
91	  }
92	
93	  return [...byId.values()]
94	    .sort((a, b) => a.timestamp.getTime() - b.timestamp.getTime())
95	    .slice(0, limit)
96	}
97
```

```text
1	import {

6	
7	/**
8	 * Fetch events within a specified time range, with pagination
9	 * @param startYear Starting year for the query
10	 * @param endYear Ending year for the query
11	 * @param limit Maximum number of records to return
12	 */
13	export async function getEventsByTimeChunk(
14	  startYear: number = 1940,
15	  endYear: number = new Date().getFullYear(),
16	  limit: number = 100
17	) {
18	  try {
19	    const start = `${startYear}-01-01T00:00:00Z`;
20	    const end = `${endYear}-12-31T23:59:59Z`;
21	
22	    return await getEventsByDateRange(start, end, limit);
23	  } catch (error) {
24	    console.error('Error fetching events by time chunk:', error);
25	    return [];
26	  }
27	}
28	
29	/**
30	 * Get aggregate statistics for events based on time range
31	 */
32	export async function getEventsStats(
33	  startYear: number = 1940,
34	  endYear: number = new Date().getFullYear()
35	) {
36	  try {
37	    const start = `${startYear}-01-01T00:00:00Z`;
38	    const end = `${endYear}-12-31T23:59:59Z`;
39	    const sql = getSql();
40	
41	    // category is a text[] column — unnest to count per category value
42	    const categoryRows = await sql`
43	      SELECT cat AS category, count(*)::int AS count
44	      FROM events,
45	           LATERAL unnest(category) AS cat
46	      WHERE date >= ${start}::timestamptz AND date <= ${end}::timestamptz
47	        AND category IS NOT NULL
48	      GROUP BY cat
49	      ORDER BY count DESC
50	    ` as { category: string; count: number }[];
51	
52	    const timeSeriesRows = await aggregateEventsByYear(start, end);
53	
54	    const locationRows = await sql`
55	      SELECT location, count(*)::int AS count
56	      FROM events
57	      WHERE date >= ${start}::timestamptz AND date <= ${end}::timestamptz
58	        AND location IS NOT NULL
59	      GROUP BY location
60	      ORDER BY count DESC
61	    ` as { location: string; count: number }[];
62	
63	    return {
64	      total: timeSeriesRows.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.count, 0),
65	      categoryDistribution: categoryRows,
66	      timeseriesData: timeSeriesRows,
67	      locationData: locationRows,
68	      timeRange: {
69	        startYear,
70	        endYear
71	      }
72	    };
73	  } catch (error) {
74	    console.error('Error fetching events stats:', error);
75	    return {
76	      total: 0,
77	      categoryDistribution: [],
78	      timeseriesData: [],
79	      locationData: [],
80	      timeRange: {
81	        startYear,
82	        endYear
83	      }
84	    };
85	  }
86	}
```

Simulate the exact stratified fetch against the real database

```bash
cd packages/db && node --input-type=module -e "
import {neon} from '@neondatabase/serverless'
import fs from 'node:fs'
const url = fs.readFileSync('.env','utf8').match(/^DATABASE_URL=[\"']?([^\"'\n]+)/m)[1]
const sql = neon(url)
const DECADE=10, MAX_WINDOWS=24, startYear=100, endYear=2026, limit=400
const span=Math.max(1,endYear-startYear+1)
const windowSize=Math.ceil(span/MAX_WINDOWS/DECADE)*DECADE || DECADE
const windows=[]
const first=Math.floor(startYear/windowSize)*windowSize
for(let y=first;y<=endYear;y+=windowSize){
  const from=Math.max(startYear,y), to=Math.min(endYear,y+windowSize-1)
  if(from<=to) windows.push({from,to})
}
const perWindow=Math.max(20,Math.ceil(limit/windows.length))
console.log('windowSize',windowSize,'windows',windows.length,'perWindow',perWindow)
const pad=y=>String(y).padStart(4,'0')
const batches=await Promise.all(windows.map(({from,to})=>
  sql.query('select id,name,date,latitude,longitude,description from events where date >= \$1::timestamptz and date <= \$2::timestamptz order by date desc limit \$3',
    [pad(from)+'-01-01T00:00:00Z', pad(to)+'-12-31T23:59:59Z', perWindow])))
const byId=new Map()
for(const b of batches) for(const r of b) byId.set(r.id,r)
const all=[...byId.values()].sort((a,b)=>new Date(a.date)-new Date(b.date)).slice(0,limit)
console.log('TOTAL fetched:', all.length)
console.log('geolocated  :', all.filter(r=>r.latitude!=null&&r.longitude!=null).length)
console.log('documented  :', all.filter(r=>(r.description||'').trim()).length)
console.log('earliest    :', all[0].name.replace(/\s+/g,' '), '|', all[0].date.toISOString().slice(0,10))
console.log('latest      :', all.at(-1).name.replace(/\s+/g,' '), '|', all.at(-1).date.toISOString().slice(0,10))
"
```

```text
207	}) {

209	  const setInteractionMode = useSpacetimeStore((s) => s.setInteractionMode)
210	  const scrollProgress = useSpacetimeStore((s) => s.scrollProgress)
211	  const cursor = useSpacetimeStore((s) => s.temporalCursor)
212	
213	  const cursorLabel =
214	    cursor.mode === 'range'
215	      ? `${cursor.start} → ${cursor.end}`
216	      : cursor.mode === 'station'
217	        ? cursor.stationId
218	        : cursor.timestamp.slice(0, 10)
219	
220	  return (
221	    <>
222	      <div className='pointer-events-auto absolute top-4 left-4'>
223	        <TemporalDial />
224	      </div>
225	
226	      <div className='pointer-events-auto absolute top-4 right-4 flex flex-col items-end gap-2'>
227	        <div className='rounded-xl border border-white/10 bg-black/60 px-3 py-2 font-mono text-[10px] text-neutral-300 backdrop-blur'>
228	          <div className='text-neutral-500'>MODE</div>
229	          <div className='flex gap-2'>
230	            {(['guided', 'free'] as const).map((m) => (
231	              <button
232	                key={m}
233	                type='button'
234	                onClick={() => setInteractionMode(m)}
235	                className={cn(
236	                  'uppercase tracking-wider',
237	                  mode === m ? 'text-amber-200' : 'text-neutral-500 hover:text-neutral-300',
238	                )}
239	              >
240	                {m}
241	              </button>
242	            ))}
243	          </div>
244	        </div>
245	        {meta ? (
246	          <div className='rounded-xl border border-white/10 bg-black/60 px-3 py-2 font-mono text-[10px] text-neutral-300 backdrop-blur'>
247	            <div className='text-neutral-500'>BOUNDED LOAD</div>
248	            <div>
249	              {meta.geolocatedCount}/{meta.total} geolocated · {meta.range}
250	            </div>
251	          </div>
252	        ) : null}
253	      </div>
254	
255	      <div className='pointer-events-none absolute bottom-4 left-4 rounded-xl border border-white/10 bg-black/60 px-3 py-2 font-mono text-[10px] text-neutral-300 backdrop-blur'>
256	        <div className='text-neutral-500'>CURSOR · SCROLL</div>
257	        <div>
258	          {cursorLabel} · {(scrollProgress * 100).toFixed(0)}%
259	        </div>
260	      </div>
261	
262	      <EvidenceLayersPanel />
263	      <EventInspector />
264	    </>
265	  )
266	}
267	
268	function metaFromResult(result: LoadSpacetimeEventsResult) {
269	  return {
270	    geolocatedCount: result.geolocatedCount,
271	    total: result.events.length,
272	    range: `${result.timeRange.startYear}–${result.timeRange.endYear}`,
273	  }
274	}
275	
276	/**
277	 * Product Spacetime Canvas — M0 shell.
278	 * Globe in the fixed slot; guided narrative as CSS 3D descent; dial beside.
279	 *
280	 * Prefer `initialData` from the server page so first paint isn't empty.
281	 * Falls back to a client fetch if omitted.
282	 */
283	export function SpacetimeCanvas({
284	  initialData,
285	}: {
286	  initialData?: LoadSpacetimeEventsResult
287	}) {
288	  const setEvents = useSpacetimeStore((s) => s.setEvents)
289	  const setStations = useSpacetimeStore((s) => s.setStations)
290	  const [meta, setMeta] = useState<{
291	    geolocatedCount: number
292	    total: number
293	    range: string
294	  } | null>(initialData ? metaFromResult(initialData) : null)
295	  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null)
296	  const [pending, startTransition] = useTransition()
297	  const didHydrate = useRef(false)
298	
299	  // Synchronous first-paint hydrate so SSR/CSR narrative isn't empty.
300	  // Zustand module state does not cross the RSC/client boundary — re-run on client.
301	  if (initialData?.events?.length && !didHydrate.current) {
302	    useSpacetimeStore.setState({
303	      events: initialData.events,
304	      stations: initialData.stations,
305	    })
306	    didHydrate.current = true
307	  }
308	
309	  // Effect hydrate covers Strict Mode remounts + client navigations where the
310	  // render-time seed did not stick; falls back to a bounded fetch if needed.
311	  useEffect(() => {
312	    if (initialData?.events?.length) {
313	      setEvents(initialData.events)
314	      setStations(initialData.stations)
315	      setMeta(metaFromResult(initialData))
316	      setError(null)
317	      return
318	    }
319	
320	    startTransition(async () => {
321	      try {
322	        const result = await loadSpacetimeEvents({
323	          startYear: 1940,
324	          endYear: new Date().getUTCFullYear(),
325	          limit: 400,
326	        })
327	        setEvents(result.events)
328	        setStations(result.stations)
329	        setMeta(metaFromResult(result))
330	        setError(null)
331	      } catch (err) {
332	        console.error(err)
333	        setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Failed to load spacetime events')
334	      }
335	    })
336	  }, [initialData, setEvents, setStations])
337	
338	  return (
339	    <>
340	      <SpacetimeCanvasShell
341	        background={<SpacetimeGlobe />}
342	        narrative={<GuidedNarrative />}
343	        chrome={<CanvasChrome meta={meta} />}
344	      />
345	      {pending && !meta ? (
346	        <div className='pointer-events-none fixed inset-x-0 top-0 z-50 flex justify-center pt-3'>
347	          <span className='rounded-full border border-white/10 bg-black/70 px-3 py-1 font-mono text-[10px] tracking-widest text-neutral-300 uppercase'>
348	            Loading bounded events…
349	          </span>
350	        </div>
351	      ) : null}
352	      {error ? (
353	        <div className='fixed inset-x-0 top-3 z-50 flex justify-center'>
354	          <span className='rounded-full border border-rose-400/30 bg-rose-950/80 px-3 py-1 text-xs text-rose-100'>
355	            {error}
356	          </span>
357	        </div>
358	      ) : null}
359	    </>
360	  )
361	}
```

```text
## 8. Spec drift worth knowing

### 8a. Measured against the storyboards

The four concept boards in [`docs/vision/storyboards/`](../vision/storyboards/) were read after this review was first written (see §10). They change three readings below.

**First, what is *not* drift.** Concepts 03 (Temporal Compare) and 04 (Flap Playback) are entirely unbuilt — no seam, no pinned frames, no playback controls, no AI synthesis. That is **correct sequencing, not drift**: they are M3/M4, and plan §4 says in as many words *"Do not start M2–M4 work during M0."* They are listed here only so the board-to-build inventory is complete.

**Concept 01 — shipped, but thinner than boarded:**

| Boarded (concept-01) | Shipped |
|---|---|
| 4 evidence layers, each with an eye toggle | `evidence-layers-panel.tsx:15-22` — 8 rows declared, **1 available** (`sightings`); 7 render disabled |
| Adaptive dial: curved milestone ladder (1945·1947·**1952**·1967·1980·2004) over a fine tick track, with a **DENSITY** legend (Sparse/Moderate/Dense) | `temporal-dial.tsx` (86 lines) — straight ladder. Density *is* encoded (`:57,:74` — opacity `0.15 + d*0.85`, `scaleX`), but there is no legend explaining it and no milestone clustering |
| Event Inspector: DATE · **LOCAL TIME ~22:00** · **SOURCES 128 / VIEW ALL** · **CREDIBILITY 72%** ring gauge · **CLAIMS (SUMMARY)** with a per-claim epistemic dot · TAGS · bookmark | `EventInspector` (`spacetime-canvas.tsx`) — type·precision, title, date, location, one epistemic sentence, summary, provenance line. **No source count, no credibility figure, no claims list, no tags.** Deliberately: the code comment at `:20` explains the 55% credibility figure was *removed* as false precision |
| Relationship arcs across the globe (visible in frames 1–2) | None. `arc` appears in the feature only in `README.md` and `types/spacetime.ts` |
| Live coordinate / `ALT 35,786 KM` / UTC readout; compass, ±zoom, recenter controls | None of the map chrome exists — and per **Break 1** the globe accepts no input at all |
| Dial spans the **bottom**, full width (as does spec §9's ASCII layout) | `spacetime-canvas.tsx:222` — `absolute top-4 left-4`, a vertical rail. Plan §1 relocated it (*"the left rail, already present as a year ladder"*) to match the v0 reference page, not the board |

The inspector does carry the plan §3 lever discipline as visible copy — *"Reconstruction requires the lever — scroll is not intent."* Credit where due.

**Concept 02 — the navigation device was substituted.** This is the sharpest board finding. Concept 02 frame 2 shows waypoints placed *on the globe* (1 1942 Manhattan Project → 2 1947 Roswell → 3 1961 Malmstrom → 4 1980 Rendlesham → 5 2004 Nimitz) driven by a horizontal **WAYPOINT NAVIGATOR** strip with an **AUTO-ADVANCE** toggle. What shipped is a **vertical `preserve-3d` scroll of event cards**.

**No board shows a scroll narrative.** Checked specifically against the frame most likely to contradict this — Concept 02 frame 4, "SYNCHRONIZED VIEW" — which turns out to *reinforce* it: a docked three-panel layout whose chapter advance is an explicit prev/next control (`‹ CURRENT CHAPTER 1947 – ROSWELL INCIDENT ›`) over a **horizontally** paging source tray. All four boards show a full-bleed globe with persistent chrome — left icon rail, layer panel, bottom temporal instrument, right inspector — which is also exactly spec §9's "Primary interaction layout" ASCII. The scroll architecture entered through plan §1, sourced from a *different* artifact (the v0 `timeline-explorer` page inspected 2026-08-01), and plan §1 then asserts it *"unifies three storyboarded concepts into one surface."* Against the boards, that unification holds for Concept 01 (globe as fixed background) but substitutes Concept 02's device rather than porting it.

**This is not "they built the wrong thing."** The user's one-line spec explicitly asked for it — *"bake it into this 3d scroll through UI if possoble"* — and a user message outranks a board. The finding is narrower and more useful than that:

> **Both shipped breaks are seam defects of the substituted architecture.** Break 2 (scroll↔station mismatch) cannot exist unless scroll drives the cursor. Break 1 is the `z-10` narrative layer sitting over a `pointer-events-none` globe. Neither failure mode exists in the boarded layout, where the globe is the foreground and the chrome is docked around it. The seam plan §1 identified as the whole point — *"the globe drops into the `.fixed.inset-0` slot"* — is precisely where both defects live. It deserves a deliberate re-examination, not another patch.

### 8b. Process and framing drift

- **The product framing is the assistant's, not the user's.** The user's entire spec was one message: *"youll see the use of the term 'spacetime canvas' i love this - esp. as a correlary to our 'research canvas' … bake it into this 3d scroll through UI **if possoble**."* The "sibling canvas, same verb, orthogonal axis" architecture was elaboration, later hardened into the plan as "deliberate and load-bearing." The conditional "if possoble" became an architectural mandate.
- **Only M0 ever had acceptance criteria.** M1–M4 are one-line scope statements with no tasks, files, or exit gates. "M1 complete" was never measurable — which is what made retroactive redefinition possible.
- **The claim that resized Foundation was never verified.** A subagent's finding — "`/api/disclosure/uap-sightings` already does year-range querying… **This shrinks the Foundation milestone**" — flowed subagent → canon → user summary with no confirming command in the main thread.
- **T-048 / Lane A / provenance backfill appear nowhere in the 08-01 session.** Not a spec-time blocker; discovered later. (Not evidence it's fabricated — the origin spec never audited data availability at all.)
- **Unenforced hard constraints to check:** the "lever" rules (plan §3 — "scroll **never** triggers generation") and temporal layer correctness (§3.4 — "a military base must not appear before it existed"). Both flagged non-negotiable; neither *enforced* in code yet. The lever rule is currently **vacuously satisfied** — no generation path exists to violate it — and the inspector copy noted in §8a (*"Reconstruction requires the lever"*) demonstrates intent, not enforcement. Both become live constraints at M2.
```

```text
## 1. Product concept

A full-screen research instrument for navigating documented sightings, historical anomalies, military
developments, nuclear events, testimony, places, and generated reconstructions across space and time.

The user is not looking at points on a map. They are moving through a **changing evidence field**:

- Where reports occurred.
- When clusters emerged.
- Which facilities, technologies, governments, witnesses, and historical events surrounded them.
- What the location plausibly looked like at the time.
- Which parts of that reconstruction are documented, inferred, disputed, or synthetic.
```

```text
1	---

10	# Design Registers — not two product lines
11	
12	Captured 2026-07-09 from a direct conversation with the product owner, who wrote most of
13	this app and was correcting an over-formalized "two aesthetics" framing. This is a light
14	map, not a governance doc — the product is a work in progress and surfaces are expected
15	to blend registers, not pick one and stay there.
16	
17	## The reframe
18	
19	There are not two competing design languages ("the app" vs. "the research canvas").
20	There are **two content registers** that coexist, often on the same surface, because the
21	subject matter itself is both:
22	
23	- **Techno-analytical register** — coordinates, space, nodes, weapons, subatomic physics,
24	  relationship graphs, AI inference overlays. Sci-fi, techie, futuristic, HUD/OSINT-leaning.
25	  This is where the 3D work belongs: `apps/app/src/features/3d/scroll-through-3d/`,
26	  `spatial-gallery`, `3d-graph`, `spherical-connection-graph` already exist as substrate —
27	  largely unwired into Timeline/Personnel/Sightings today.
28	- **Archival-material register** — paper, grain, aged edges, stamps, redaction, typewriter
29	  text. Historical, academic, archival, because the subject matter (declassified files,
30	  testimony, case records) demands it. Shipped today as Microfilm Dark on the Research
31	  Canvas (partial chrome sketch in non-canonical root `DESIGN.md`).
32	
33	A single surface can and often should carry both — e.g. a sighting report is an archival
34	*document* (register 2) about a spatial/physical *event* (register 1). Don't force a
35	surface to pick one.
36	
37	## The unifying primitive: document materiality
38	
39	The thing that should travel everywhere, not just the Canvas: a shared "paper/texture"
40	treatment for anything that renders as a file, record, or evidence object — classified or
41	declassified. Microfilm Dark already has the pieces (film grain via inline SVG
42	feTurbulence, warm dot grid, redaction-bar skeleton loading states, clipped dossier
43	corners) but they're implemented canvas-local. The open work, when it's time, is
44	extracting that into a shared primitive so Timeline events, personnel dossiers, and
45	sighting reports can adopt the same paper feel without re-deriving it — this is what
46	"parity" actually means here, not a mode taxonomy.
47	
48	## Tiering note
49	
50	The Research Canvas is the power-user surface — deep investigation, AI-assisted
51	synthesis, real cost (LLM inference). The rest of the app (Timeline, key-figures,
52	sightings, history) serves a broader, less committed audience. This has a design
53	consequence: the AI-inference visual language (dashed provenance borders, evidentiary
54	badges) is a Canvas-tier signal, not something the general surfaces need to inherit
55	wholesale — they may stay closer to pure archival-material register with lighter or no
56	AI overlay. Membership/cost gating on the Canvas is a product decision that sits outside
57	design scope but should inform which surfaces earn the AI-overlay treatment.
58	
59	## What this doc is not
60	
61	Not a mode registry, not an audit, not a mandate to reconcile `(site)/timeline` vs.
62	`research-canvas/views/timeline` right now (that duplication exists and is real, but is
63	separate cleanup work, not a design-identity question). Not a claim that the
64	techno-analytical and archival-material registers need formal names or a picker UI.
65
```

```text
4	export interface BuildStationsOptions {

13	/**
14	 * Build adaptive temporal stations from event density.
15	 *
16	 * - historical: decade ticks across the corpus range
17	 * - event: densest days / notable years from the loaded events
18	 *
19	 * Investigation stations are generated later from a selected case (M4).
20	 */
21	export function buildTemporalStations(
22	  events: SpacetimeEvent[],
23	  options: BuildStationsOptions = {},
24	): TemporalStation[] {
25	  const {
26	    includeHistoricalDecades = true,
27	    historicalStartYear = 1940,
28	    historicalEndYear = new Date().getUTCFullYear(),
29	    maxEventStations = 24,
30	  } = options
31	
32	  const stations: TemporalStation[] = []
33	
34	  if (includeHistoricalDecades) {
35	    const startDecade = Math.floor(historicalStartYear / 10) * 10
36	    const endDecade = Math.floor(historicalEndYear / 10) * 10
37	    for (let year = startDecade; year <= endDecade; year += 10) {
38	      stations.push({
39	        id: `historical-${year}`,
40	        kind: 'historical',
41	        label: `${year}s`,
42	        timestamp: `${year}-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`,
43	        density: 0,
44	      })
45	    }
46	  }
47	
48	  // Bucket events by UTC day, then pick top days per decade so the
49	  // guided narrative spans history instead of collapsing into one flap.
50	  const byDay = new Map<string, SpacetimeEvent[]>()
51	  for (const event of events) {
52	    const day = event.timestamp.slice(0, 10)
53	    if (!/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(day)) continue
54	    const bucket = byDay.get(day) ?? []
55	    bucket.push(event)
56	    byDay.set(day, bucket)
57	  }
58	
59	  const scoredDays = [...byDay.entries()].map(([day, dayEvents]) => ({
60	    day,
61	    dayEvents,
62	    decade: Math.floor(Number(day.slice(0, 4)) / 10) * 10,
63	    score: dayEvents.length + dayEvents.reduce((s, e) => s + (e.credibilityScore ?? 0.2), 0),
64	  }))
65	
66	  const byDecade = new Map<number, typeof scoredDays>()
67	  for (const entry of scoredDays) {
68	    const bucket = byDecade.get(entry.decade) ?? []
69	    bucket.push(entry)
70	    byDecade.set(entry.decade, bucket)
71	  }
72	
73	  const perDecade = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(maxEventStations / Math.max(1, byDecade.size)))
74	  const rankedDays = [...byDecade.values()]
75	    .flatMap((entries) =>
76	      [...entries].sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score).slice(0, perDecade),
77	    )
78	    .sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score)
79	    .slice(0, maxEventStations)
80	
81	  const maxScore = rankedDays[0]?.score ?? 1
82	
83	  for (const {day, dayEvents, score} of rankedDays) {
84	    const year = day.slice(0, 4)
85	    const label =
86	      dayEvents.length === 1
87	        ? (dayEvents[0]?.title ? truncateAtWordBoundary(dayEvents[0].title, 42) : day)
88	        : `${dayEvents.length} events · ${year}`
89	
90	    stations.push({
91	      id: `event-${day}`,
92	      kind: 'event',
93	      label,
94	      timestamp: `${day}T12:00:00.000Z`,
95	      density: score / maxScore,
96	      eventIds: dayEvents.map((e) => e.id),
97	    })
98	  }
99	
100	  // Stamp historical densities from year counts
101	  const byYear = new Map<number, number>()
102	  for (const event of events) {
103	    const year = Number(event.timestamp.slice(0, 4))
104	    if (!Number.isFinite(year)) continue
105	    byYear.set(year, (byYear.get(year) ?? 0) + 1)
106	  }
107	  const maxYearCount = Math.max(1, ...byYear.values())
108	
109	  for (const station of stations) {
110	    if (station.kind !== 'historical') continue
111	    const decade = Number(station.id.replace('historical-', ''))
112	    let count = 0
113	    for (let y = decade; y < decade + 10; y++) count += byYear.get(y) ?? 0
114	    station.density = count / maxYearCount
115	  }
116	
117	  return stations.sort(
118	    (a, b) => new Date(a.timestamp).getTime() - new Date(b.timestamp).getTime(),
119	  )
120	}
121	
122	/** Map a 0–1 scroll/dial progress onto the nearest station. */
123	export function stationAtProgress(
124	  stations: TemporalStation[],
125	  progress: number,
126	): TemporalStation | null {
127	  if (stations.length === 0) return null
128	  const clamped = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, progress))
129	  const idx = Math.min(stations.length - 1, Math.round(clamped * (stations.length - 1)))
130	  return stations[idx] ?? null
131	}
```

```typescript
'use client'

import {useSyncExternalStore} from 'react'
import type mapboxgl from 'mapbox-gl'

/**
 * Registry for the single live Mapbox instance.
 *
 * The docked map controls (compass, zoom, recenter) and the coordinate readout
 * sit *outside* the globe component in the boarded layout, so they need a handle
 * on the map. This is a module-level ref rather than Zustand state on purpose:
 * a Mapbox `Map` is a large mutable object with its own event loop, and putting
 * it in the store would make every consumer of the store a subscriber to it.
 *
 * `useSpacetimeMap()` re-renders only on attach/detach, which is all the
 * controls need to flip between disabled and live.
 */

let mapInstance: mapboxgl.Map | null = null
const listeners = new Set<() => void>()

export function registerSpacetimeMap(map: mapboxgl.Map | null): void {
  mapInstance = map
  for (const listener of listeners) listener()
}

export function getSpacetimeMap(): mapboxgl.Map | null {
  return mapInstance
}

function subscribe(listener: () => void): () => void {
  listeners.add(listener)
  return () => {
    listeners.delete(listener)
  }
}

/** Server snapshot is always null — the map only exists in the browser. */
const serverSnapshot = () => null

export function useSpacetimeMap(): mapboxgl.Map | null {
  return useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, () => mapInstance, serverSnapshot)
}
```

```tsx
import Link from 'next/link'
import {BarChart3, Eye, FolderClosed, Globe2, Settings, Sparkles} from 'lucide-react'

/**
 * Left instrument rail — concept-01 frame 1 / concept-03 frame 1.

 * The boards show six labelled icon slots (OVERVIEW · SIGHTINGS · EVENTS ·
 * CASES · ANALYTICS · SETTINGS). Slots that correspond to a real route link to
 * it; the two that don't render visibly inert rather than as dead links —
 * chrome that looks live but does nothing is worse than chrome that says so.
 */

  label: string
  icon: typeof Globe2
  href?: string
  /** True for the surface we are currently on. */
  active?: boolean
}

  {label: 'Sightings', icon: Eye, href: '/sightings'},
  {label: 'Events', icon: Sparkles, href: '/events'},
  {label: 'Cases', icon: FolderClosed, href: '/tours'},
  {label: 'Analytics', icon: BarChart3},
  {label: 'Settings', icon: Settings},
]

export function SpacetimeRail() {
  return (
    <nav
      aria-label='Observatory sections'
      className='flex h-full flex-col items-center gap-1 border-r border-[rgba(125,190,210,0.16)] bg-[rgba(6,10,13,0.9)] py-4'

              className={cn(

              )}
            />
            <span
              className={cn(
                'font-mono text-[7px] tracking-[0.16em] uppercase transition-colors',

              )}
            >
              {item.label}
            </span>
          </>
        )

        const shell = cn(
          'group relative flex w-14 flex-col items-center gap-1.5 rounded-lg px-1 py-2.5',
          item.active
            ? 'bg-[rgba(79,216,232,0.09)] ring-1 ring-[rgba(79,216,232,0.28)]'
            : 'hover:bg-white/[0.04]',
        )

        if (!item.href) {
          return (
            <div
              key={item.label}
              className={cn(shell, 'cursor-not-allowed opacity-35')}
              title={`${item.label} — no surface built yet`}
              aria-disabled
            >
              {body}
            </div>

        return (
          <Link
            key={item.label}
            href={item.href}
            className={shell}

              />

            {body}
          </Link>
        )
      })}
    </nav>
  )
}
```

```tsx
'use client'

import {Maximize2, MoveDiagonal, Orbit} from 'lucide-react'
import {cn} from '@/lib/utils'
import {useSpacetimeStore} from '../state/spacetime-store'

export interface SpacetimeTopbarProps {
  /** Loaded-corpus readout: what the bounded query actually returned. */
  meta: {geolocatedCount: number; total: number; range: string} | null
  visibleCount: number
}

/**
 * Observatory header — concept-01 frame 1's `ULTRATERRESTRIAL /
 * TEMPORAL OBSERVATORY` lockup plus the right-hand action cluster.
 *
 * Two deliberate accommodations to the app's global chrome, which is
 * `fixed top-6 left-6` (wordmark) and `fixed top-6 right-6` (hamburger) from
 * `MenuTrigger` in the root layout:
 *
 *   - The wordmark is not repeated here. It already sits in this band, so the
 *     header opens with the *sub*-lockup and leaves `pl-[13.5rem]` for it.
 *     Two "ULTRATERRESTRIAL" marks 40px apart would read as a bug.
 *   - `pr-[4.5rem]` keeps the action cluster clear of the hamburger.
 */
export function SpacetimeTopbar({meta, visibleCount}: SpacetimeTopbarProps) {
  const mode = useSpacetimeStore((s) => s.interactionMode)
  const setInteractionMode = useSpacetimeStore((s) => s.setInteractionMode)

  return (
    <header className='flex h-full items-center gap-4 border-b border-[rgba(125,190,210,0.16)] bg-[rgba(6,10,13,0.92)] pr-[4.5rem] pl-[13.5rem]'>
      <span aria-hidden className='h-6 w-px bg-[rgba(125,190,210,0.22)]' />

      <div className='min-w-0'>
        <p className='font-mono text-[10px] tracking-[0.3em] text-[#4fd8e8] uppercase'>
          Temporal Observatory
        </p>
        <p className='mt-0.5 truncate font-mono text-[9px] tracking-[0.16em] text-[#4d5c62] uppercase'>
          Spacetime Canvas · curated events corpus
        </p>
      </div>

      <div className='ml-auto flex items-center gap-2'>
        {meta ? (
          <div className='hidden items-center gap-4 rounded-lg border border-[rgba(125,190,210,0.16)] bg-[rgba(8,13,17,0.7)] px-3 py-1.5 lg:flex'>
            <Readout label='On canvas' value={`${visibleCount}/${meta.total}`} />
            <Readout label='Mapped' value={`${meta.geolocatedCount}`} />
            <Readout label='Span' value={meta.range} />
          </div>
        ) : null}

        {/*
         * Mode is a real switch, not decoration: `guided` gives scroll authority
         * over the temporal cursor, `free` gives it to the dial. Keeping it in
         * the header (rather than a floating card) is what the boards show for
         * global state.
         */}
        <div className='flex items-center gap-px overflow-hidden rounded-lg border border-[rgba(125,190,210,0.16)]'>
          {(['guided', 'free'] as const).map((m) => (
            <button
              key={m}
              type='button'
              onClick={() => setInteractionMode(m)}
              className={cn(
                'px-2.5 py-1.5 font-mono text-[9px] tracking-[0.18em] uppercase transition-colors',
                mode === m
                  ? 'bg-[rgba(79,216,232,0.14)] text-[#4fd8e8]'
                  : 'bg-[rgba(8,13,17,0.7)] text-[#5d6d74] hover:text-[#a8b8be]',
              )}
              aria-pressed={mode === m}
            >
              {m}
            </button>
          ))}
        </div>

        <IconButton label='Reset camera to the whole corpus' icon={Orbit} action='reset' />
        <IconButton label='Fit the mapped records in view' icon={MoveDiagonal} action='fit' />
        <IconButton label='Toggle full screen' icon={Maximize2} action='fullscreen' />
      </div>
    </header>
  )
}

function Readout({label, value}: {label: string; value: string}) {
  return (
    <span className='flex flex-col leading-tight'>
      <span className='font-mono text-[8px] tracking-[0.2em] text-[#4d5c62] uppercase'>
        {label}
      </span>
      <span className='font-mono text-[10px] text-[#c3d3d8]'>{value}</span>
    </span>
  )
}

/**
 * Header actions. `reset` / `fit` drive the map through the registry; there is
 * no icon here that does nothing — the boards' remaining glyphs (help, share)
 * are omitted rather than mocked.
 */
function IconButton({
  label,
  icon: Icon,
  action,
}: {
  label: string
  icon: typeof Orbit
  action: 'reset' | 'fit' | 'fullscreen'
}) {
  const onClick = () => {
    if (action === 'fullscreen') {
      const shell = document.querySelector('[data-spacetime-shell]')
      if (!(shell instanceof HTMLElement)) return
      if (document.fullscreenElement) void document.exitFullscreen()
      else void shell.requestFullscreen().catch(() => {})
      return
    }
    // Dispatched on the shell so the globe — which owns the Mapbox camera —
    // stays the only thing that moves it. See spacetime-globe.tsx.
    document
      .querySelector('[data-spacetime-shell]')
      ?.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('spacetime:camera', {detail: {action}}))
  }

  return (
    <button
      type='button'
      onClick={onClick}
      title={label}
      aria-label={label}
      className='flex h-8 w-8 items-center justify-center rounded-lg border border-[rgba(125,190,210,0.16)] bg-[rgba(8,13,17,0.7)] text-[#6b7c83] transition-colors hover:border-[rgba(79,216,232,0.4)] hover:text-[#4fd8e8]'
    >
      <Icon size={14} strokeWidth={1.6} />
    </button>
  )
}
```

```tsx
'use client'

import {useMemo, useState} from 'react'
import {Play} from 'lucide-react'
import {cn} from '@/lib/utils'
import {niceYearStep} from '../lib/temporal-stations'
import {useSpacetimeStore} from '../state/spacetime-store'
import type {SpacetimeEvent, TemporalStation} from '../types/spacetime'

/**
 * Adaptive temporal dial — concept-01 frame 2, docked full width at the bottom
 * as in spec §9's layout, with concept-04's density track underneath.
 *
 * Three things the board shows that this has to earn rather than draw:
 *
 * 1. **Milestone chips over a fine tick ruler.** Chips are the densest event
 *    stations, thinned so two never collide; ticks are round years from
 *    `niceYearStep`.
 * 2. **A density track.** Concept-04's "CLUSTER TIMELINE" histogram. Bars are
 *    real per-year record counts, not decoration.
 * 3. **"Adaptive."** The corpus runs 196 CE → present, so a linear axis over the
 *    whole range crushes every modern milestone into the last few percent of the
 *    width — unreadable, and the board's 1900–2024 span never had to face it.
 *    The dial therefore opens on the *dense era* (the window holding ~92% of
 *    records) and collects the deep-time tail into a leading bracket you can
 *    click to widen the domain. The bracket states its own count, so nothing is
 *    hidden — it is scoped, and says so.
 */

/** Fraction of records the default (dense) domain must contain. */
const DENSE_COVERAGE = 0.92
/** Minimum axis separation between two chips, as a fraction of the width. */
const MIN_CHIP_GAP = 0.075
const MAX_CHIPS = 9

function yearOf(timestamp: string): number {
  return Number(timestamp.slice(0, 4))
}

export function TemporalDial({className}: {className?: string}) {
  const stations = useSpacetimeStore((s) => s.stations)
  const events = useSpacetimeStore((s) => s.events)
  const cursor = useSpacetimeStore((s) => s.temporalCursor)
  const setTemporalCursor = useSpacetimeStore((s) => s.setTemporalCursor)
  const setInteractionMode = useSpacetimeStore((s) => s.setInteractionMode)
  const selectEvent = useSpacetimeStore((s) => s.selectEvent)

  const [showFullRange, setShowFullRange] = useState(false)

  const years = useMemo(
    () => events.map((e) => yearOf(e.timestamp)).filter(Number.isFinite).sort((a, b) => a - b),
    [events],
  )

  const domain = useMemo(() => computeDomain(years, showFullRange), [years, showFullRange])
  const outsideCount = useMemo(
    () => years.filter((y) => y < domain.start).length,
    [years, domain.start],
  )

  const ticks = useMemo(() => buildTicks(domain), [domain])
  const histogram = useMemo(() => buildHistogram(years, domain), [years, domain])

  const activeStationId = cursor.mode === 'station' ? cursor.stationId : null
  const cursorYear =
    cursor.mode === 'range' ? yearOf(cursor.start) : yearOf(cursor.timestamp)

  const chips = useMemo(
    () => selectChips(stations, domain),
    [stations, domain],
  )

  const onSelect = (station: TemporalStation) => {
    // Dial input is an explicit override — flip to free so scroll stops
    // fighting it for the cursor (store contract D1).
    setInteractionMode('free')
    setTemporalCursor({
      mode: 'station',
      stationId: station.id,
      timestamp: station.timestamp,
    })
    // A station that resolves to exactly one record *is* that record; opening
    // the inspector is what a user means by clicking it.
    const only = station.eventIds?.length === 1 ? station.eventIds[0] : null
    selectEvent(only ?? null)
  }

  const hasData = events.length > 0

  return (
    <section
      aria-label='Adaptive temporal dial'
      className={cn(
        'relative border-t border-[rgba(125,190,210,0.16)] bg-[rgba(6,10,13,0.94)] px-5 pt-3 pb-4',
        className,
      )}
    >
      <div className='flex items-center gap-3'>
        <span className='rounded-md border border-[rgba(125,190,210,0.22)] px-2 py-1 font-mono text-[8px] tracking-[0.22em] text-[#7d8f95] uppercase'>
          Adaptive temporal dial
        </span>

        {outsideCount > 0 || showFullRange ? (
          <button
            type='button'
            onClick={() => setShowFullRange((v) => !v)}
            className='rounded-md border border-[rgba(240,168,96,0.32)] bg-[rgba(240,168,96,0.08)] px-2 py-1 font-mono text-[8px] tracking-[0.16em] text-[#f0a860] uppercase transition-colors hover:bg-[rgba(240,168,96,0.16)]'
          >
            {showFullRange
              ? `Focus ${dense(years)}–${domain.end}`
              : `+ ${outsideCount} before ${domain.start}`}
          </button>
        ) : null}

        <p className='ml-auto flex items-baseline gap-2'>
          <span className='font-mono text-[8px] tracking-[0.22em] text-[#4d5c62] uppercase'>
            Cursor
          </span>
          <span className='font-mono text-[12px] tracking-wide text-[#4fd8e8]'>
            {cursor.mode === 'range'
              ? `${cursor.start.slice(0, 10)} → ${cursor.end.slice(0, 10)}`
              : cursor.timestamp.slice(0, 10)}
          </span>
        </p>

        {/*
         * LIVE on the boards streams present-day activity. Nothing streams yet,
         * so this jumps the cursor to the most recent record instead of
         * pretending to be a feed — same affordance, no false claim.
         */}
        <button
          type='button'
          disabled={!hasData}
          onClick={() => {
            const latest = [...events].sort(
              (a, b) => new Date(b.timestamp).getTime() - new Date(a.timestamp).getTime(),
            )[0]
            if (!latest) return
            setInteractionMode('free')
            setTemporalCursor({mode: 'exact', timestamp: latest.timestamp, precision: latest.timePrecision})
            selectEvent(latest.id)
          }}
          title='Jump to the most recent record in the corpus'
          className='flex items-center gap-1.5 rounded-md border border-[rgba(125,190,210,0.24)] bg-[rgba(8,13,17,0.8)] px-2.5 py-1.5 font-mono text-[9px] tracking-[0.2em] text-[#a8b8be] uppercase transition-colors hover:border-[rgba(79,216,232,0.45)] hover:text-[#4fd8e8] disabled:opacity-30'
        >
          Latest
          <Play size={9} strokeWidth={2} />
        </button>
      </div>

      {/* ---- axis ------------------------------------------------------- */}
      <div className='relative mt-3 h-[76px]'>
        {/* chips */}
        {chips.map((chip) => {
          const active = chip.station.id === activeStationId
          return (
            <button
              key={chip.station.id}
              type='button'
              onClick={() => onSelect(chip.station)}
              title={chip.station.label}
              style={{left: `${chip.position * 100}%`}}
              className='absolute top-0 -translate-x-1/2'
            >
              <span
                className={cn(
                  'flex items-center justify-center rounded-full border font-mono transition-all',
                  active
                    ? 'h-9 w-9 border-[#4fd8e8] bg-[rgba(79,216,232,0.18)] text-[11px] text-[#dff8fb] shadow-[0_0_18px_rgba(79,216,232,0.45)]'
                    : 'h-7 w-[52px] border-[rgba(125,190,210,0.3)] bg-[rgba(8,13,17,0.9)] text-[10px] text-[#a8b8be] hover:border-[rgba(79,216,232,0.6)] hover:text-[#dff8fb]',
                )}
              >
                {yearOf(chip.station.timestamp)}
              </span>
              {/* drop-line to the track, as on the board */}
              <span
                aria-hidden
                className={cn(
                  'absolute left-1/2 w-px -translate-x-1/2',
                  active ? 'bg-[#4fd8e8]' : 'bg-[rgba(125,190,210,0.28)]',
                )}
                style={{top: active ? 36 : 28, height: active ? 12 : 20}}
              />
            </button>
          )
        })}

        {/* density track — concept-04 cluster timeline */}
        <div className='absolute inset-x-0 bottom-[18px] flex h-6 items-end gap-px'>
          {histogram.map((bin) => (
            <span
              key={bin.year}
              title={`${bin.year}–${bin.year + bin.step - 1} · ${bin.count} record${bin.count === 1 ? '' : 's'}`}
              className='flex-1 rounded-sm bg-[#4fd8e8]'
              style={{
                height: `${Math.max(bin.count > 0 ? 8 : 2, bin.intensity * 100)}%`,
                opacity: bin.count > 0 ? 0.28 + bin.intensity * 0.62 : 0.12,
              }}
            />
          ))}
        </div>

        {/* baseline + tick ruler */}
        <div className='absolute inset-x-0 bottom-[16px] h-px bg-[rgba(125,190,210,0.3)]' />
        {ticks.map((tick) => (
          <div
            key={tick.year}
            className='absolute bottom-0 -translate-x-1/2'
            style={{left: `${tick.position * 100}%`}}
          >
            <span
              aria-hidden
              className='mx-auto block h-[5px] w-px bg-[rgba(125,190,210,0.4)]'
            />
            <span className='mt-1 block font-mono text-[8px] tracking-wider text-[#4d5c62] whitespace-nowrap'>
              {tick.year}
            </span>
          </div>
        ))}

        {/* live cursor position on the axis */}
        {Number.isFinite(cursorYear) &&
        cursorYear >= domain.start &&
        cursorYear <= domain.end ? (
          <span
            aria-hidden
            className='absolute bottom-[10px] h-[34px] w-px bg-[#4fd8e8] shadow-[0_0_10px_rgba(79,216,232,0.8)]'
            style={{left: `${((cursorYear - domain.start) / domain.span) * 100}%`}}
          />
        ) : null}
      </div>

      {!hasData ? (
        <p className='absolute inset-x-0 bottom-8 text-center font-mono text-[9px] tracking-[0.2em] text-[#4d5c62] uppercase'>
          Awaiting corpus…
        </p>
      ) : null}
    </section>
  )
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

interface Domain {
  start: number
  end: number
  span: number
}

function dense(years: number[]): number {
  if (years.length === 0) return 1900
  const idx = Math.floor(years.length * (1 - DENSE_COVERAGE))
  const pivot = years[Math.min(idx, years.length - 1)] ?? years[0]!
  return Math.floor(pivot / 50) * 50
}

function computeDomain(years: number[], full: boolean): Domain {
  const nowYear = new Date().getUTCFullYear()
  if (years.length === 0) return {start: 1900, end: nowYear, span: nowYear - 1900}

  const end = Math.max(years[years.length - 1] ?? nowYear, nowYear)
  const min = years[0] ?? 1900
  const start = full ? Math.floor(min / 50) * 50 : Math.max(Math.floor(min / 50) * 50, dense(years))

  return {start, end, span: Math.max(1, end - start)}
}

function buildTicks(domain: Domain): Array<{year: number; position: number}> {
  const step = niceYearStep(domain.span, 10)
  const first = Math.ceil(domain.start / step) * step
  const ticks: Array<{year: number; position: number}> = []
  for (let year = first; year <= domain.end; year += step) {
    ticks.push({year, position: (year - domain.start) / domain.span})
  }
  return ticks
}

/**
 * Bin record counts across the domain. Bin width is chosen so the track keeps
 * ~72 bars regardless of span — dense enough to read as a distribution, coarse
 * enough that a single record doesn't render as a 1px sliver.
 */
function buildHistogram(
  years: number[],
  domain: Domain,
): Array<{year: number; step: number; count: number; intensity: number}> {
  const binCount = 72
  const step = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(domain.span / binCount))
  const bins: Array<{year: number; step: number; count: number; intensity: number}> = []

  for (let year = domain.start; year <= domain.end; year += step) {
    const count = years.filter((y) => y >= year && y < year + step).length
    bins.push({year, step, count, intensity: 0})
  }

  const peak = Math.max(1, ...bins.map((b) => b.count))
  for (const bin of bins) bin.intensity = bin.count / peak
  return bins
}

/**
 * Thin event stations down to chips that will not collide.
 *
 * Greedy by density: take the busiest station first and reject anything closer
 * than `MIN_CHIP_GAP` on the axis. Sorting the survivors back into time order
 * matters — the boards read left to right as a chronology.
 */
function selectChips(
  stations: TemporalStation[],
  domain: Domain,
): Array<{station: TemporalStation; position: number}> {
  const candidates = stations
    .filter((s) => s.kind === 'event')
    .map((station) => ({
      station,
      position: (yearOf(station.timestamp) - domain.start) / domain.span,
    }))
    .filter((c) => c.position >= 0 && c.position <= 1)
    .sort((a, b) => (b.station.density ?? 0) - (a.station.density ?? 0))

  const accepted: Array<{station: TemporalStation; position: number}> = []
  for (const candidate of candidates) {
    if (accepted.length >= MAX_CHIPS) break
    if (accepted.some((a) => Math.abs(a.position - candidate.position) < MIN_CHIP_GAP)) {
      continue
    }
    accepted.push(candidate)
  }

  return accepted.sort((a, b) => a.position - b.position)
}

export type {SpacetimeEvent}
```
