247	## Bulk Ingestion (`scripts/bulk_folder_ingestion.py`)
248	
249	Supports PDF, DOCX, TXT, MD files. Extracts text, creates triple-RAG documents.
250	
251	**CLI entry point — choose one:**
252	
253	```bash
254	# Option A: Interactive TUI (recommended for first use)
255	python cli.py
256	# → Select "Bulk Ingestion" from menu → enter folder path when prompted
257	
258	# Option B: Run script directly (non-interactive)
259	python scripts/bulk_folder_ingestion.py
260	# Note: no built-in CLI flags — configure folder_path in the script or use Option C
261	
262	# Option C: Python one-liner
263	python -c "
264	from scripts.bulk_folder_ingestion import BulkFolderIngestion
265	b = BulkFolderIngestion('/path/to/folder')
266	docs = b.discover_documents()
267	print(f'Found {len(docs)} files')
268	for d in docs: b.create_triple_rag_document(d, b.extract_text_content(d))
269	"
270	```
271	
272	**Python API:**
273	
274	```python
275	from scripts.bulk_folder_ingestion import BulkFolderIngestion
276	
277	ingestion = BulkFolderIngestion(folder_path, output_dir="ingestion_results")
278	docs = ingestion.discover_documents()           # find all supported files
279	for doc in docs:
280	    text = ingestion.extract_text_content(doc)  # PDF/DOCX/TXT/MD
281	    rag_doc = ingestion.create_triple_rag_document(doc, text)
282	```
283	
284	## Playlist Ingestion (`scripts/playlist_ingestion.py`)
285	
286	Batch-ingest one or more YouTube podcast playlists end-to-end. Each episode flows through: enumeration → transcript fetch → parse/clean → **fidelity review** (quality gate) → full pipeline (KB storage, NER entity extraction, vectorization, CocoIndex knowledge graph, Mem0).
287	
288	```bash
289	# One or more playlist URLs (plain video URLs also accepted)
290	python scripts/playlist_ingestion.py "https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL..." [MORE_URLS...]
291	
292	# From a file (one URL per line, # comments allowed), with vector store upload
293	python scripts/playlist_ingestion.py --from-file playlists.txt --upload
294	
295	# Preview a new playlist's caption quality without ingesting
296	python scripts/playlist_ingestion.py <URL> --limit 5 --dry-run
297	
298	# Stricter gate + LLM coherence pass (FIDELITY_REVIEW_MODEL, default gpt-5.5)
299	python scripts/playlist_ingestion.py <URL> --min-fidelity 0.6 --llm-review
300	```
301	
302	Flags: `--upload` (OpenAI vector store), `--no-kb`, `--limit N` (per playlist), `--force` (reprocess done episodes), `--dry-run`, `--min-fidelity 0.45`, `--llm-review`, `--delay 2.0` (seconds between episodes), `--state-file PATH`.
303	
304	**Resume is automatic**: state is checkpointed to `data/playlist_ingestion/state.json` after every episode; re-runs skip `ingested`/`quarantined` episodes and retry `failed`/`no_transcript` ones.
305	
306	**Fidelity review** (`lib/transcript_fidelity.py`) scores each transcript 0–1 from coverage, speech density (wpm), caption gaps, artifact ratio, and repetition; verdicts: `pass` ≥ 0.7, `review` ≥ 0.45, `fail` < 0.45. Failing/below-threshold episodes are **quarantined** (transcript + fidelity JSON kept on disk, not ingested). Artifacts: cleaned transcripts in `data/playlist_ingestion/transcripts/`, per-episode fidelity reports and per-run markdown summaries in `data/playlist_ingestion/reports/`.
307	
308	See [Playlist ingestion details](references/playlist-ingestion.md) for stage internals, state schema, quarantine review workflow, and tuning.
309	
310	## Content Type Detection
311	
312	YouTube: URL contains `youtube.com` or `youtu.be`. Web: starts with `http(s)://`. File: everything else (validated with `os.path.exists`).
313

```text
1	# Playlist Ingestion Reference
2	
3	Deep-dive on the YouTube podcast playlist pipeline (`scripts/playlist_ingestion.py`).
4	
5	## Stage-by-Stage Flow
6	
7	```
8	playlist URL(s)
9	  |-> Episode Enumeration
10	  |     yt-dlp flat extraction (no downloads; returns id, title, duration per entry)
11	  |     pytube fallback if yt-dlp fails
12	  |     Plain video URLs are treated as single-episode playlists
13	  |
14	  |-> Transcript Fetch (per episode)
15	  |     lib/youtube_transcript_enhanced.get_metadata_and_transcript_api_first()
16	  |     Cookie-free youtube-transcript-api + oEmbed metadata
17	  |     Returns a `reason` code, mapped to a status:
18	  |       no captions / captions disabled -> `no_transcript`  (retried next run)
19	  |       private / deleted / age-gated   -> `unavailable`     (terminal)
20	  |       YouTube blocked this IP         -> `blocked`         (retried; see below)
21	  |
22	  |-> Parse + Clean
23	  |     lib/transcript_fidelity.clean_transcript()
24	  |     Strips [Music]/[Applause]/[inaudible] cues, dedupes stuck caption
25	  |     lines, normalizes whitespace
26	  |     Cleaned copy saved to data/playlist_ingestion/transcripts/<video_id>.txt
27	  |
28	  |-> Fidelity Review
29	  |     lib/transcript_fidelity.review_transcript() -> FidelityReport
30	  |     Heuristic subscores (weights):
31	  |       coverage   .30  captions cover the episode's yt-dlp duration
32	  |       density    .20  words-per-minute in the 90-220 speech band
33	  |       gaps       .15  largest silence between caption segments
34	  |       artifacts  .15  non-speech cue ratio in raw text
35	  |       repetition .20  duplicate 6-gram windows (stuck captions)
36	  |     Optional --llm-review: samples 3 chunks, asks FIDELITY_REVIEW_MODEL
37	  |     (default gpt-5.5) for a coherence rating that becomes 1/3 of the score
38	  |     Verdicts: pass >= 0.7 | review 0.45-0.7 | fail < 0.45
39	  |     Report saved to data/playlist_ingestion/reports/<video_id>.fidelity.json
40	  |
41	  |-> Quality Gate
42	  |     verdict `fail` OR score < --min-fidelity -> status `quarantined`
43	  |     (transcript + report kept on disk for human review; NOT ingested)
44	  |
45	  |-> Full Pipeline (main.process_url)
46	        KB storage -> Upstash sync -> NER entity extraction ->
47	        vectorization (--upload -> OpenAI vector store) ->
48	        CocoIndex knowledge graph -> Mem0 memory
49	```
50	
51	## Checkpointing & Resume
52	
53	State lives in `data/playlist_ingestion/state.json`, keyed by video ID:
54	
55	```json
56	{
57	  "videos": {
58	    "dQw4w9WgXcQ": {
59	      "title": "...", "url": "...", "playlist_id": "PL...",
60	      "status": "ingested", "fidelity": 0.87, "doc_id": "abc123",
61	      "updated": "2026-07-23T18:00:00+00:00"
62	    }
63	  }
64	}
65	```
66	
67	- State is written after **every** episode (atomic tmp-file swap), so a crash
68	  or Ctrl-C loses at most the in-flight episode.
69	- Re-running the same playlist skips episodes whose status is `ingested`,
70	  `quarantined`, or `unavailable` (terminal). `no_transcript`, `blocked`,
71	  `enrichment_failed`, and `failed` episodes are retried automatically. Use
72	  `--force` to reprocess everything.
73	- Statuses: `ingested`, `quarantined`, `unavailable`, `no_transcript`,
74	  `blocked`, `enrichment_failed`, `failed`, `dry_run`, `skipped` (counted per
75	  run, not stored).
76	
77	## IP Blocks
78	
79	YouTube rate-limits the caption endpoint per IP. A block is a property of the
80	**run**, not of a video, so after `YT_BLOCKED_ABORT_THRESHOLD` consecutive
81	`blocked` episodes (default 3) the run aborts with exit code 2 rather than
82	walking the rest of the playlist and recording every episode as a failure.
83	Blocked episodes are not terminal — fix egress and re-run.
84	
85	Remedies, in `.env` or the environment:
86	
87	```bash
88	YT_WEBSHARE_PROXY_USERNAME=...   # Webshare rotating residential (preferred)
89	YT_WEBSHARE_PROXY_PASSWORD=...
90	YT_PROXY_URL=http://user:pass@host:port   # or any single HTTP(S) proxy
91	YT_TRANSCRIPT_MAX_RETRIES=2      # per-video retries when blocked (proxy only)
92	YT_TRANSCRIPT_BACKOFF=5          # seconds before the first retry
93	YT_BLOCKED_ABORT_THRESHOLD=3     # consecutive blocks before aborting the run
94	```
95	
96	Without a proxy the fetcher does **not** retry: the same blocked IP would fail
97	every attempt, so retrying only slows the run down before it aborts.
98	
99	## Output Artifacts
100	
101	| Path | Contents |
102	|------|----------|
103	| `data/playlist_ingestion/state.json` | Resume checkpoint (all episodes ever seen) |
104	| `data/playlist_ingestion/transcripts/<id>.txt` | Cleaned transcript (title + URL header) |
105	| `data/playlist_ingestion/reports/<id>.fidelity.json` | Full FidelityReport with subscores + issues |
106	| `data/playlist_ingestion/reports/run-<ts>.md` | Per-run markdown summary table |
107	
108	## Duplicate Fetch Note
109	
110	The fidelity stage fetches the transcript once for scoring, then
111	`main.process_url()` re-fetches it internally during ingestion. This is
112	deliberate: it keeps `main.py` untouched and the gate fully decoupled. The
113	transcript API is fast and the `--delay` flag (default 2s) keeps request
114	pacing polite. If YouTube rate-limits a long run, raise `--delay`.
115	
116	## Reviewing Quarantined Episodes
117	
118	```bash
119	# List quarantined episodes with their issues
120	python -c "
121	import json
122	s = json.load(open('data/playlist_ingestion/state.json'))
123	for vid, e in s['videos'].items():
124	    if e.get('status') == 'quarantined':
125	        print(f\"{vid}  {e.get('fidelity')}  {e['title'][:60]}\")
126	        for i in e.get('issues', []): print(f'   - {i}')
127	"
128	```
129	
130	To ingest one anyway after manual review, run the standard single-URL path:
131	
132	```bash
133	python main.py "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=<id>" --upload
134	```
135	
136	then update its state entry (or just leave it — `--force` is per-run, and the
137	single-URL path doesn't consult the playlist state file).
138	
139	## Tuning
140	
141	- `--min-fidelity 0.6` — stricter gate for noisy auto-captioned channels
142	- `--llm-review` — worth it for channels with heavy crosstalk; costs one
143	  chat completion per episode (`FIDELITY_REVIEW_MODEL`, default `gpt-5.5`)
144	- `--limit 5 --dry-run` — cheap preview of a new playlist's caption quality
145	  before committing to a full ingest
146	- Fidelity weights/thresholds live at the top of `lib/transcript_fidelity.py`
147
```

78	## Data Flow Details
79	
80	### YouTube Processing Path
81	
82	```
83	URL -> is_youtube_url() check
84	  -> process_youtube_url_enhanced() [lib/knowledge_base_service.py]
85	    -> YouTube transcript extraction [lib/youtube.py]
86	    -> Content analysis + summarization
87	    -> add_youtube_to_knowledge_base() -> doc_id
88	    -> Upstash Search sync (IntegratedUpstashSyncer)
89	  -> Mem0: add_web_article_memory() [skipped for YT, handled in transcript]
90	  -> CocoIndex: trigger_cocoindex_processing(doc_id)
91	  -> Mem0: add_processing_summary_memory()
92	```
93	
94	### Web URL Processing Path
95	
96	```
97	URL -> process_web_url_enhanced() [lib/knowledge_base_service.py]
98	  -> WebContentProcessor.process() [processing/web_content_processor.py]
99	  -> Content analysis + classification
100	  -> add_to_knowledge_base() -> doc_id
101	  -> Upstash Search sync
102	-> Mem0: add_web_article_memory(title, url, content, summary, tags)
103	-> CocoIndex: trigger_cocoindex_processing(doc_id)
104	-> Mem0: add_processing_summary_memory()
105	```
106	
107	### File Processing Path
108	
109	```
110	File -> process_file() [main.py]
111	  -> Read file content
112	  -> Extract title from filename or markdown header
113	  -> OpenAI upload (if --upload)
114	  -> Upstash queue (add_processed_content_to_queue)
115	  -> add_to_knowledge_base() -> doc_id
116	  -> Mem0: add_file_content_memory()
117	  -> Entity extraction: process_summary_file_interactive(path, doc_id, interactive=False)
118	  -> CocoIndex: trigger_cocoindex_processing(doc_id)
119	  -> File relocation: processing_queue/ -> packages/knowledge-base/sources/files/
120	  -> Mem0: add_processing_summary_memory()
121	```
122	
123	## Integration Status Check
124	
125	`python main.py --status` reports on:
126	
127	| Backend | Check |
128	|---------|-------|
129	| Local KB | KnowledgeBaseCRUD initialized |
130	| Search Sync | IntegratedUpstashSyncer available |
131	| Search URL | UPSTASH_SEARCH_URL env var set |
132	| Search Token | UPSTASH_SEARCH_TOKEN env var set |
133	| CocoIndex KG | cocoindex module importable |
134	| KG Statistics | Documents, entities, relationships counts |
135	| Mem0 | MEM0_API_KEY set and module available |
136	
137	## Triple RAG Architecture
138	
139	The system uses three vector backends with weighted scoring:
140	
141	| Backend | Weight | Package | Purpose |
142	|---------|--------|---------|---------|
143	| Upstash Vector | 40% | lib/upstash/vector.py | Cloud vector search |
144	| FAISS (LocalRAG) | 40% | vector_storage/ | Local vector indices |
145	| CocoIndex PostgreSQL | 20% | lib/cocoindex_integration.py | Knowledge graph analytics |
146	
147	Orchestrated by `lib/unified_rag_orchestrator.py`.
148	
149	## Entity Extraction System
150	
151	Located in `lib/entity_extraction/`:
152	
153	- **Schemas**: Define entity types (personnel, organizations, locations, events, technologies, documents)
154	- **Processors**: `interactive_entity_processor.py` -- extracts entities and matches against 230,998+ Xata database records
155	- **Tools**: Utilities for entity normalization, deduplication
156	- **85-95% extraction accuracy** on UAP research content
157	
158	Key function:
159	```python
160	from lib.entity_extraction.processors.interactive_entity_processor import process_summary_file_interactive
161	results = process_summary_file_interactive(summary_path, doc_id, interactive=False)
162	# Returns: { total_entities, total_matches, entities: [...], status }
163	```
164	
165	## Knowledge Base CRUD API
166	
167	```python
168	from lib.knowledge_base_crud import KnowledgeBaseCRUD
169	kb = KnowledgeBaseCRUD()
170	
171	# Core operations
172	doc_id = kb.add_document(data, doc_type)    # doc_type: 'research', 'case_file', etc.
173	doc = kb.get_document(doc_id)
174	results = kb.search_documents(query)         # Returns: [{ title, score, doc_type, snippet }]
175	stats = kb.get_statistics()                  # Returns: { total_documents, total_tags, documents_by_type, popular_tags, last_updated }

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	YouTube Playlist Ingestion Pipeline
4	
5	Takes one or more YouTube podcast playlist URLs, enumerates every episode,
6	and drives each one through the full Disclosure RAG pipeline:
7	
8	  playlist URL(s)
9	    -> episode enumeration (yt-dlp flat extraction, pytube fallback)
10	    -> transcript fetch (lib/youtube_transcript_enhanced, cookie-free)
11	    -> transcript parse + clean (lib/transcript_fidelity.clean_transcript)
12	    -> fidelity review (lib/transcript_fidelity.review_transcript, optional LLM pass)
13	    -> quality gate (fail/below threshold -> quarantined for human review)
14	    -> main.process_url() -> KB storage, Upstash sync, NER entity extraction,
15	       vectorization (--upload -> OpenAI vector store), CocoIndex knowledge
16	       graph, Mem0 memory
17	
18	Every episode outcome is checkpointed to a state file, so re-running the same
19	playlist resumes where it left off. Per-episode transcripts and fidelity
20	reports are saved under data/playlist_ingestion/ alongside a markdown run
21	report.
22	
23	Usage (from apps/disclosure-rag/, venv active, .env loaded):
24	
25	  python scripts/playlist_ingestion.py <PLAYLIST_URL> [<PLAYLIST_URL> ...]
26	  python scripts/playlist_ingestion.py --from-file playlists.txt --upload
27	  python scripts/playlist_ingestion.py <URL> --limit 5 --dry-run
28	  python scripts/playlist_ingestion.py <URL> --llm-review --min-fidelity 0.6
29	  python scripts/playlist_ingestion.py <URL> --force        # reprocess all
30	"""
31	
32	import argparse
33	import json
34	import logging
35	import os
36	import re
37	import sys
38	import time
39	from datetime import datetime, timezone
40	from pathlib import Path
41	from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional
42	
43	sys.path.append(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
44	
45	from lib.transcript_fidelity import clean_transcript, review_transcript
46	
47	logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s")
48	logger = logging.getLogger("playlist_ingestion")
49	
50	BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
51	OUTPUT_DIR = BASE_DIR / "data" / "playlist_ingestion"
52	DEFAULT_STATE_FILE = OUTPUT_DIR / "state.json"
53	
54	# Terminal states that --force is required to reprocess. `unavailable` is here
55	# because a private/deleted video does not come back: re-listing it on every run
56	# spends a request that counts against the same quota that gets us IP-blocked.
57	DONE_STATUSES = {"ingested", "quarantined", "unavailable"}
58	
59	# Transcript failure reason -> episode status. Anything unmapped (missing
60	# captions, disabled captions) stays `no_transcript`, which is retryable.
61	REASON_STATUS = {
62	    "blocked": "blocked",
63	    "private": "unavailable",
64	    "unavailable": "unavailable",
65	    "age_restricted": "unavailable",
66	}
67	
68	# Consecutive `blocked` episodes after which the run aborts. YouTube blocks an
69	# IP, not a video, so once it starts every remaining episode fails too — the
70	# previous behaviour marched through 104 videos and recorded 55 of them as
71	# `no_transcript`, which reads as "these podcasts have no captions" forever.
72	BLOCKED_ABORT_THRESHOLD = int(os.getenv("YT_BLOCKED_ABORT_THRESHOLD", "3"))
73	
74	
75	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- enumeration
76	
77	# YouTube video IDs are exactly 11 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_-]. Playlist/channel IDs
78	# (PL…, UU…, OL…, RD…, LL…, FL…, UC…) are longer, so length alone separates
79	# them — this is the guard that catches a container ID leaking into a video slot.
80	VIDEO_ID_RE = re.compile(r"^[\w-]{11}$")
81	
82	
83	def is_video_id(value: Any) -> bool:
84	    return isinstance(value, str) and bool(VIDEO_ID_RE.match(value))
85	
86	
87	def enumerate_playlist(playlist_url: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
88	    """Return {playlist_id, title, videos: [{video_id, url, title, duration}]}.
89	
90	    Tries yt-dlp flat extraction first (fast, no per-video downloads), then
91	    falls back to pytube. A plain video URL is treated as a single-episode
92	    playlist.
93	    """
94	    try:
95	        import yt_dlp
96	        opts = {
97	            "quiet": True, "no_warnings": True,
98	            "extract_flat": "in_playlist",   # flatten entries; still resolve the container
99	            "skip_download": True,
100	            # We only ever want metadata. Without these, processing a bare video
101	            # URL aborts on format selection ("Requested format is not
102	            # available") before any metadata comes back.
103	            "ignore_no_formats_error": True,
104	            "format": None,
105	        }
106	        with yt_dlp.YoutubeDL(opts) as ydl:
107	            # NOTE: process=False must NOT be used here. For a playlist URL it
108	            # returns an unresolved {_type: "url", id: <PLAYLIST_ID>} stub with
109	            # no "entries" key, which the single-video fallback below then
110	            # mistakes for a video — sending the playlist ID down the pipeline
111	            # as a video ID. Processing resolves the stub into real entries;
112	            # extract_flat keeps it cheap (no per-video format resolution).
113	            info = ydl.extract_info(playlist_url, download=False)
114	        if info.get("_type") == "playlist":
115	            entries = list(info.get("entries") or [])
116	        elif info.get("_type") in (None, "video"):
117	            entries = [info]  # genuine single video
118	        else:
119	            raise ValueError(f"unresolved yt-dlp result: _type={info.get('_type')!r}")
120	        videos = []
121	        for e in entries:
122	            if not e:
123	                continue
124	            vid = e.get("id")
125	            if not is_video_id(vid):
126	                logger.warning(f"Skipping entry with non-video id {vid!r} ({e.get('title')!r})")
127	                continue
128	            videos.append({
129	                "video_id": vid,
130	                "url": f"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={vid}",
131	                "title": e.get("title") or vid,
132	                "duration": e.get("duration"),
133	                "uploader": e.get("uploader") or e.get("channel"),
134	            })
135	        return {
136	            "playlist_id": info.get("id") or "unknown",
137	            "title": info.get("title") or playlist_url,
138	            "videos": videos,
139	        }
140	    except Exception as e:
141	        logger.warning(f"yt-dlp enumeration failed ({e}); trying pytube")
142	
143	    try:
144	        from pytube import Playlist
145	        pl = Playlist(playlist_url)
146	        videos = []
147	        for url in pl.video_urls:
148	            m = re.search(r"[?&]v=([\w-]+)", url)
149	            if m and is_video_id(m.group(1)):
150	                videos.append({"video_id": m.group(1), "url": url, "title": m.group(1), "duration": None,
151	                               "uploader": None})
152	        return {"playlist_id": getattr(pl, "playlist_id", "unknown"),
153	                "title": getattr(pl, "title", playlist_url), "videos": videos}
154	    except Exception as e:
155	        logger.error(f"Could not enumerate playlist {playlist_url}: {e}")
156	        return {"playlist_id": "unknown", "title": playlist_url, "videos": []}
157	
158	
159	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- state
160	
161	def load_state(state_file: Path) -> Dict[str, Any]:
162	    if state_file.exists():
163	        try:
164	            return json.loads(state_file.read_text())
165	        except Exception as e:
166	            logger.warning(f"State file unreadable, starting fresh: {e}")
167	    return {"videos": {}}
168	
169	
170	def save_state(state: Dict[str, Any], state_file: Path) -> None:
171	    state_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
172	    tmp = state_file.with_suffix(".tmp")
173	    tmp.write_text(json.dumps(state, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
174	    tmp.replace(state_file)
175	
176	
177	#: Per-attempt outcome keys. Cleared before each write so a later failed
178	#: attempt can't inherit an earlier success's fields — a `no_transcript` retry
179	#: was leaving the prior run's `fidelity` and `doc_id` in place, which reads as
180	#: though a fetch that never happened had produced a document.
181	_OUTCOME_KEYS = ("fidelity", "fidelity_verdict", "doc_id", "rag_status", "error", "issues")
182	
183	
184	def record(state: Dict[str, Any], video: Dict[str, Any], playlist_id: str, **fields) -> None:
185	    entry = state["videos"].setdefault(video["video_id"], {})
186	    for key in _OUTCOME_KEYS:
187	        entry.pop(key, None)
188	    entry.update({
189	        "title": video.get("title"),
190	        "url": video.get("url"),
191	        "playlist_id": playlist_id,
192	        "updated": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
193	        **fields,
194	    })
195	
196	
197	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- per-episode
198	
199	def fetch_transcript(url: str) -> tuple:
200	    """Fetch transcript + metadata via the cookie-free transcript-api path.
201	
202	    Returns (result | None, reason). The reason is what lets the caller tell an
203	    episode with no captions from an IP block, which is a run-level condition.
204	    """
205	    try:
206	        from lib.youtube_transcript_enhanced import get_metadata_and_transcript_api_first
207	        result = get_metadata_and_transcript_api_first(url)
208	        if result.get("ok") and result.get("transcript"):
209	            return result, "ok"
210	        return None, result.get("reason") or "no_captions"
211	    except Exception as e:
212	        logger.warning(f"Transcript fetch failed for {url}: {e}")
213	        return None, "error"
214	
215	
216	def _enrichment_outcome(result: Dict[str, Any]) -> tuple:
217	    """Grade LLM enrichment from a process_url result: (status, error_detail).
218	
219	    The status lives in a different place depending on which path ran:
220	    `process_file` sets `result['rag_pipeline']` and `result['metadata']
221	    ['rag_pipeline']`, while the YouTube path (lib/youtube.py) files it under
222	    the transcript's file metadata and surfaces it as a `stage_report` entry.
223	
224	    Returns "unknown" when no signal is found. That matters: reporting
225	    `ingested` on absence is precisely how a run of documents whose
226	    enrichment had 401'd got recorded as successful.
227	    """
228	    for container in (result, result.get("metadata") or {}, result.get("file_metadata") or {}):
229	        rag = container.get("rag_pipeline") if isinstance(container, dict) else None
230	        if isinstance(rag, dict) and rag.get("status"):
231	            return rag["status"], "; ".join(rag.get("errors") or [])[:300]
232	
233	    for stage in result.get("stage_report") or []:
234	        if isinstance(stage, dict) and "RAG prompt pipeline" in (stage.get("name") or ""):
235	            raw = stage.get("status") or "unknown"
236	            return {"success": "ok", "failed": "error"}.get(raw, raw), (stage.get("detail") or "")[:300]
237	
238	    return "unknown", ""
239	
240	
241	def process_episode(video: Dict[str, Any], playlist_id: str, state: Dict[str, Any],
242	                    args: argparse.Namespace, transcripts_dir: Path, reports_dir: Path) -> str:
243	    """Run one episode through fetch -> parse -> fidelity gate -> pipeline.
244	
245	    Returns the resulting status string.
246	    """
247	    vid, url = video["video_id"], video["url"]
248	
249	    fetched, reason = fetch_transcript(url)
250	    if not fetched:
251	        status = REASON_STATUS.get(reason, "no_transcript")
252	        record(state, video, playlist_id, status=status, error=f"transcript {reason}")
253	        return status
254	
255	    raw_transcript = fetched["transcript"]
256	    cleaned = clean_transcript(raw_transcript)
257	    transcripts_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
258	    (transcripts_dir / f"{vid}.txt").write_text(
259	        f"{fetched.get('title') or video['title']}\n{url}\n\n{cleaned}", encoding="utf-8")
260	
261	    fidelity = review_transcript(
262	        transcript=raw_transcript,
263	        video_id=vid,
264	        segments=fetched.get("transcript_segments"),
265	        expected_duration_seconds=video.get("duration"),
266	        use_llm=args.llm_review,
267	    )
268	    reports_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
269	    (reports_dir / f"{vid}.fidelity.json").write_text(
270	        json.dumps(fidelity.to_dict(), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
271	
272	    logger.info(f"  fidelity {fidelity.score:.2f} ({fidelity.verdict}) — {video['title'][:70]}")
273	
274	    if fidelity.verdict == "fail" or fidelity.score < args.min_fidelity:
275	        record(state, video, playlist_id, status="quarantined",
276	               fidelity=fidelity.score, fidelity_verdict=fidelity.verdict,
277	               issues=fidelity.issues[:5])
278	        return "quarantined"
279	
280	    if args.dry_run:
281	        record(state, video, playlist_id, status="dry_run",
282	               fidelity=fidelity.score, fidelity_verdict=fidelity.verdict)
283	        return "dry_run"
284	
285	    # Full pipeline: KB storage, Upstash sync, NER, vectorize, CocoIndex KG, Mem0
286	    try:
287	        from main import process_url
288	        result = process_url(url, upload=args.upload, add_to_kb=not args.no_kb)
289	        if result and result.get("doc_id"):
290	            # A doc_id only proves the transcript was stored. LLM enrichment
291	            # (classification, NER, embeddable texts) can fail independently —
292	            # and did, silently, for a whole run when OPENAI_API_KEY was
293	            # revoked. main.py already grades that as ok|hold|rejected|error;
294	            # surface it rather than reporting every stored transcript as a
295	            # successful ingestion.
296	            rag_status, enrich_errors = _enrichment_outcome(result)
297	            if rag_status not in ("ok", "unknown"):
298	                logger.warning(
299	                    "  enrichment %s for %s — %s", rag_status, vid, enrich_errors or "no detail")
300	                record(state, video, playlist_id, status="enrichment_failed",
301	                       fidelity=fidelity.score, fidelity_verdict=fidelity.verdict,
302	                       doc_id=result["doc_id"], rag_status=rag_status,
303	                       error=enrich_errors or f"rag_pipeline status={rag_status}")
304	                return "enrichment_failed"
305	            if rag_status == "unknown":
306	                logger.warning(
307	                    "  enrichment status not reported by the pipeline for %s — "
308	                    "recording rag_status=unknown, not treating as enriched", vid)
309	            record(state, video, playlist_id, status="ingested",
310	                   fidelity=fidelity.score, fidelity_verdict=fidelity.verdict,
311	                   doc_id=result["doc_id"], rag_status=rag_status)
312	            return "ingested"
313	        record(state, video, playlist_id, status="failed",
314	               fidelity=fidelity.score, error="pipeline returned no doc_id")
315	        return "failed"
316	    except Exception as e:
317	        logger.error(f"Pipeline error for {vid}: {e}")
318	        record(state, video, playlist_id, status="failed",
319	               fidelity=fidelity.score, error=str(e))
320	        return "failed"
321	
322	
323	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- run report
324	
325	def write_run_report(runs: List[Dict[str, Any]], counts: Dict[str, int], reports_dir: Path) -> Path:
326	    ts = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")
327	    lines = [f"# Playlist Ingestion Run — {ts} UTC", ""]
328	    lines.append("| Status | Count |")
329	    lines.append("|--------|-------|")
330	    for status, n in sorted(counts.items()):
331	        lines.append(f"| {status} | {n} |")
332	    lines.append("")
333	    for run in runs:
334	        lines.append(f"## {run['title']} (`{run['playlist_id']}`)")
335	        lines.append("")
336	        lines.append("| Episode | Status | Fidelity | Enrichment | Doc ID |")
337	        lines.append("|---------|--------|----------|------------|--------|")
338	        for ep in run["episodes"]:
339	            lines.append(
340	                f"| {ep['title'][:60]} | {ep['status']} | {ep.get('fidelity', '—')} "
341	                f"| {ep.get('rag_status', '—')} | {ep.get('doc_id', '—')} |")
342	        lines.append("")
343	    reports_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
344	    path = reports_dir / f"run-{ts}.md"
345	    path.write_text("\n".join(lines), encoding="utf-8")
346	    return path
347	
348	
349	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- main
350	
351	def main() -> int:
352	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Ingest YouTube podcast playlists into the Disclosure RAG pipeline")
353	    parser.add_argument("playlists", nargs="*", help="One or more playlist (or video) URLs")
354	    parser.add_argument("--from-file", help="File with one playlist URL per line (# comments allowed)")
355	    parser.add_argument("--upload", action="store_true", help="Upload to OpenAI vector store (vectorization)")
356	    parser.add_argument("--no-kb", action="store_true", help="Skip knowledge base storage")
357	    parser.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=0, help="Max new episodes to process per playlist")
358	    parser.add_argument("--force", action="store_true", help="Reprocess episodes already in the state file")
359	    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="Fetch + fidelity-review only; no ingestion")
360	    parser.add_argument("--min-fidelity", type=float, default=0.45,
361	                        help="Minimum fidelity score to ingest (default 0.45; below -> quarantined)")
362	    parser.add_argument("--llm-review", action="store_true",
363	                        help="Add LLM coherence pass to fidelity review (uses FIDELITY_REVIEW_MODEL)")
364	    parser.add_argument("--delay", type=float, default=2.0, help="Seconds between episodes (default 2)")
365	    parser.add_argument("--state-file", default=str(DEFAULT_STATE_FILE), help="Checkpoint state file path")
366	    args = parser.parse_args()
367	
368	    urls = list(args.playlists)
369	    if args.from_file:
370	        for line in Path(args.from_file).read_text().splitlines():
371	            line = line.strip()
372	            if line and not line.startswith("#"):
373	                urls.append(line)
374	    if not urls:
375	        parser.error("No playlist URLs given (positional args or --from-file)")
376	
377	    state_file = Path(args.state_file)
378	    state = load_state(state_file)
379	    transcripts_dir = OUTPUT_DIR / "transcripts"
380	    reports_dir = OUTPUT_DIR / "reports"
381	
382	    counts: Dict[str, int] = {}
383	    runs: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
384	    consecutive_blocked = 0
385	    aborted = False
386	
387	    for playlist_url in urls:
388	        if aborted:
389	            break
390	        logger.info(f"Enumerating playlist: {playlist_url}")
391	        playlist = enumerate_playlist(playlist_url)
392	        videos = playlist["videos"]
393	        logger.info(f"Playlist '{playlist['title']}': {len(videos)} episodes")
394	        if not videos:
395	            counts["enumeration_failed"] = counts.get("enumeration_failed", 0) + 1
396	            continue
397	
398	        run: Dict[str, Any] = {"playlist_id": playlist["playlist_id"], "title": playlist["title"], "episodes": []}
399	        processed = 0
400	        for i, video in enumerate(videos, 1):
401	            vid = video["video_id"]
402	            existing = state["videos"].get(vid, {})
403	            if not args.force and existing.get("status") in DONE_STATUSES:
404	                logger.info(f"[{i}/{len(videos)}] skip (already {existing['status']}): {video['title'][:70]}")
405	                counts["skipped"] = counts.get("skipped", 0) + 1
406	                continue
407	            if args.limit and processed >= args.limit:
408	                logger.info(f"--limit {args.limit} reached for this playlist")
409	                break
410	
411	            logger.info(f"[{i}/{len(videos)}] processing: {video['title'][:70]}")
412	            status = process_episode(video, playlist["playlist_id"], state, args, transcripts_dir, reports_dir)
413	            counts[status] = counts.get(status, 0) + 1
414	            processed += 1
415	            save_state(state, state_file)
416	
417	            entry = state["videos"].get(vid, {})
418	            run["episodes"].append({"title": video["title"], "status": status,
419	                                    "fidelity": entry.get("fidelity"), "doc_id": entry.get("doc_id")})
420	
421	            # Only a status that required YouTube to actually serve us caption
422	            # data clears the counter. `unavailable` must not: a private video
423	            # fails before any transcript request, so treating it as evidence
424	            # that egress works lets a playlist with private episodes sprinkled
425	            # through it reset the breaker forever while every real fetch fails.
426	            if status == "blocked":
427	                consecutive_blocked += 1
428	            elif status != "unavailable":
429	                consecutive_blocked = 0
430	            if consecutive_blocked >= BLOCKED_ABORT_THRESHOLD:
431	                from lib.youtube_transcript_enhanced import proxy_configured
432	                logger.error(
433	                    "Aborting: YouTube blocked %d consecutive transcript requests. This is an "
434	                    "IP-level block, not a property of these videos — continuing would record "
435	                    "the rest of the playlist as failures. Remedy: %s, then re-run (blocked "
436	                    "episodes are not terminal and will be retried).",
437	                    consecutive_blocked,
438	                    "rotate the proxy / wait out the block" if proxy_configured()
439	                    else "set YT_WEBSHARE_PROXY_USERNAME + YT_WEBSHARE_PROXY_PASSWORD (or YT_PROXY_URL)")
440	                aborted = True
441	                break
442	
443	            if args.delay and i < len(videos):
444	                time.sleep(args.delay)
445	        runs.append(run)
446	
447	    report_path = write_run_report(runs, counts, reports_dir)
448	    logger.info(f"Run report: {report_path}")
449	    logger.info(f"Summary: {json.dumps(counts)}")
450	    if aborted:
451	        return 2
452	    return 0 if not counts.get("failed") else 1

1	"""
2	Transcript Fidelity Review
3	
4	Scores a YouTube transcript's quality before it is ingested into the
5	knowledge base. Combines cheap deterministic heuristics (coverage, speech
6	density, gaps, caption artifacts, repetition) with an optional LLM coherence
7	review. Used by scripts/playlist_ingestion.py as a quality gate.
8	
9	All functions are fault-tolerant: a scoring failure returns a neutral result
10	rather than raising, matching the pipeline's never-block philosophy.
11	"""

13	import json
14	import logging
15	import os
16	import re
17	from dataclasses import dataclass, field, asdict
18	from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional

20	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

22	# Bracketed caption cues that carry no speech content
23	CUE_PATTERN = re.compile(r"\[(?:music|applause|laughter|inaudible|foreign|__+|\s*)\]", re.IGNORECASE)
24	# Normal conversational speech falls in this words-per-minute band
25	WPM_LOW, WPM_HIGH = 90, 220
26	
27	
28	@dataclass
29	class FidelityReport:
30	    video_id: str
31	    score: float = 0.0                      # composite 0-1
32	    verdict: str = "unknown"                # pass | review | fail
33	    word_count: int = 0
34	    covered_seconds: float = 0.0
35	    expected_seconds: Optional[float] = None
36	    words_per_minute: Optional[float] = None
37	    max_gap_seconds: float = 0.0
38	    artifact_ratio: float = 0.0
39	    repetition_ratio: float = 0.0
40	    subscores: Dict[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)
41	    issues: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
42	    llm_review: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
43	
44	    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
45	        return asdict(self)

47	
48	def clean_transcript(text: str) -> str:
49	    """Normalize a raw caption transcript into readable prose.
50	
51	    Strips non-speech cues, collapses whitespace, and de-duplicates
52	    consecutive identical lines (a common auto-caption artifact).
53	    """
54	    if not text:
55	        return ""
56	    text = CUE_PATTERN.sub(" ", text)
57	    lines = [ln.strip() for ln in text.splitlines()]
58	    deduped: List[str] = []
59	    for ln in lines:
60	        if not ln:
61	            continue
62	        if deduped and ln == deduped[-1]:
63	            continue
64	        deduped.append(ln)
65	    text = " ".join(deduped)
66	    return re.sub(r"\s{2,}", " ", text).strip()
67	
68	
69	def _seg_field(seg: Any, name: str, default: float = 0.0) -> float:
70	    """Read a timing field from a transcript segment.
71	
72	    youtube-transcript-api >= 1.0 yields FetchedTranscriptSnippet objects with
73	    attributes; older versions (and our cached fixtures) yield plain dicts.
74	    Support both — an AttributeError here silently zeroed every coverage metric
75	    and left the fidelity gate passing everything on its fallback score.
76	    """
77	    value = seg.get(name, default) if hasattr(seg, "get") else getattr(seg, name, default)
78	    try:
79	        return float(value)
80	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
81	        raise ValueError(f"non-numeric {name}: {value!r}")
82	
83	
84	def _segment_stats(segments: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> Dict[str, float]:
85	    """Coverage and gap metrics from timed transcript segments."""
86	    covered_end = 0.0
87	    max_gap = 0.0
88	    prev_end = 0.0
89	    for seg in segments:
90	        try:
91	            start = _seg_field(seg, "start")
92	            duration = _seg_field(seg, "duration")
93	        except (TypeError, ValueError):
94	            continue
95	        if prev_end and start - prev_end > max_gap:
96	            max_gap = start - prev_end
97	        prev_end = max(prev_end, start + duration)
98	        covered_end = max(covered_end, start + duration)
99	    return {"covered_seconds": covered_end, "max_gap_seconds": max_gap}
100	
101	
102	def _repetition_ratio(text: str, window: int = 6) -> float:
103	    """Fraction of duplicated n-gram windows — high values mean stuck captions."""
104	    words = text.lower().split()
105	    if len(words) < window * 2:
106	        return 0.0
107	    grams = [" ".join(words[i:i + window]) for i in range(0, len(words) - window, window)]
108	    if not grams:
109	        return 0.0
110	    return 1.0 - (len(set(grams)) / len(grams))
111	
112	
113	def _taper(value: float, low: float, high: float, hard_low: float, hard_high: float) -> float:
114	    """1.0 inside [low, high], linear falloff to 0 at hard bounds."""
115	    if low <= value <= high:
116	        return 1.0
117	    if value < low:
118	        if value <= hard_low:
119	            return 0.0
120	        return (value - hard_low) / (low - hard_low)
121	    if value >= hard_high:
122	        return 0.0
123	    return (hard_high - value) / (hard_high - high)
124	
125	
126	def llm_coherence_review(text: str, video_id: str, model: Optional[str] = None,
127	                         samples: int = 3, sample_chars: int = 1500) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
128	    """Optional LLM pass: rate coherence of sampled transcript chunks 0-1.
129	
130	    Requires OPENAI_API_KEY. Returns None on any failure.
131	    """
132	    try:
133	        from openai import OpenAI
134	        client = OpenAI()
135	        model = model or os.getenv("FIDELITY_REVIEW_MODEL", "gpt-5.5")
136	
137	        step = max(1, (len(text) - sample_chars) // max(1, samples - 1)) if len(text) > sample_chars else len(text)
138	        chunks = [text[i:i + sample_chars] for i in range(0, len(text), step)][:samples]
139	
140	        prompt = (
141	            "You are reviewing machine-generated podcast transcript excerpts for fidelity. "
142	            "Rate overall coherence from 0.0 (garbled, unusable) to 1.0 (clean, fully readable), "
143	            "and list concrete issues (garbled phrases, mid-sentence truncation, wrong-language text, "
144	            "caption artifacts). Respond ONLY with JSON: "
145	            '{"coherence": <float>, "issues": [<strings>]}\n\n'
146	            + "\n---\n".join(chunks)
147	        )
148	        response = client.chat.completions.create(
149	            model=model,
150	            messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
151	        )
152	        raw = response.choices[0].message.content.strip()
153	        raw = re.sub(r"^```(?:json)?|```$", "", raw, flags=re.MULTILINE).strip()
154	        data = json.loads(raw)
155	        return {
156	            "model": model,
157	            "coherence": max(0.0, min(1.0, float(data.get("coherence", 0.5)))),
158	            "issues": [str(i) for i in data.get("issues", [])][:10],
159	        }
160	    except Exception as e:
161	        logger.warning(f"LLM coherence review skipped for {video_id}: {e}")
162	        return None
163	
164	
165	def review_transcript(
166	    transcript: str,
167	    video_id: str,
168	    segments: Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]] = None,
169	    expected_duration_seconds: Optional[float] = None,
170	    use_llm: bool = False,
171	    llm_model: Optional[str] = None,
172	) -> FidelityReport:
173	    """Score transcript fidelity 0-1 and assign a verdict.
174	
175	    Verdicts: 'pass' (>= 0.7), 'review' (0.45-0.7), 'fail' (< 0.45).
176	    """
177	    report = FidelityReport(video_id=video_id)
178	    try:
179	        raw = transcript or ""
180	        cleaned = clean_transcript(raw)
181	        words = cleaned.split()
182	        report.word_count = len(words)
183	
184	        if report.word_count < 50:
185	            report.verdict = "fail"
186	            report.issues.append(f"Transcript too short ({report.word_count} words)")
187	            return report
188	
189	        # Artifact ratio measured against the raw text before cleaning
190	        cues = len(CUE_PATTERN.findall(raw))
191	        raw_tokens = max(1, len(raw.split()))
192	        report.artifact_ratio = round(cues / raw_tokens, 4)
193	
194	        report.repetition_ratio = round(_repetition_ratio(cleaned), 4)
195	
196	        seg_stats = _segment_stats(segments or [])
197	        report.covered_seconds = round(seg_stats["covered_seconds"], 1)
198	        report.max_gap_seconds = round(seg_stats["max_gap_seconds"], 1)
199	        report.expected_seconds = expected_duration_seconds
200	
201	        # --- subscores ---
202	        subs: Dict[str, float] = {}
203	
204	        if expected_duration_seconds and report.covered_seconds:
205	            coverage = min(1.0, report.covered_seconds / expected_duration_seconds)
206	            subs["coverage"] = coverage
207	            if coverage < 0.8:
208	                report.issues.append(
209	                    f"Captions cover only {coverage:.0%} of the {expected_duration_seconds:.0f}s episode")
210	        else:
211	            subs["coverage"] = 0.75  # unknown duration: mild neutral prior
212	
213	        minutes = (report.covered_seconds or (expected_duration_seconds or 0)) / 60.0
214	        if minutes > 0.5:
215	            wpm = report.word_count / minutes
216	            report.words_per_minute = round(wpm, 1)
217	            subs["density"] = _taper(wpm, WPM_LOW, WPM_HIGH, 30, 400)
218	            if subs["density"] < 0.5:
219	                report.issues.append(f"Abnormal speech density ({wpm:.0f} wpm)")
220	        else:
221	            subs["density"] = 0.75
222	
223	        subs["gaps"] = _taper(report.max_gap_seconds, 0, 20, 0, 180)
224	        if report.max_gap_seconds > 60:
225	            report.issues.append(f"Caption gap of {report.max_gap_seconds:.0f}s detected")
226	
227	        subs["artifacts"] = max(0.0, 1.0 - report.artifact_ratio * 5)
228	        if report.artifact_ratio > 0.05:
229	            report.issues.append(f"High non-speech cue ratio ({report.artifact_ratio:.1%})")
230	
231	        subs["repetition"] = max(0.0, 1.0 - report.repetition_ratio * 4)
232	        if report.repetition_ratio > 0.15:
233	            report.issues.append(f"Repeated caption blocks ({report.repetition_ratio:.1%} duplicate n-grams)")
234	
235	        weights = {"coverage": 0.30, "density": 0.20, "gaps": 0.15, "artifacts": 0.15, "repetition": 0.20}
236	        score = sum(subs[k] * w for k, w in weights.items())
237	
238	        if use_llm:
239	            report.llm_review = llm_coherence_review(cleaned, video_id, model=llm_model)
240	            if report.llm_review:
241	                # LLM verdict counts for a third of the final score when available
242	                score = score * (2 / 3) + report.llm_review["coherence"] * (1 / 3)
243	                report.issues.extend(report.llm_review.get("issues", []))
244	
245	        report.subscores = {k: round(v, 3) for k, v in subs.items()}
246	        report.score = round(score, 3)
247	        report.verdict = "pass" if score >= 0.7 else ("review" if score >= 0.45 else "fail")
248	        return report
249	    except Exception as e:
250	        logger.warning(f"Fidelity review failed for {video_id}: {e}")
251	        report.verdict = "review"
252	        report.score = 0.5
253	        report.issues.append(f"Fidelity review error: {e}")
254	        return report

51	def _extract_json_payload(text: str) -> Any:
52	    """Parse JSON from a model response, tolerating markdown fences."""
53	    if not text:
54	        raise ValueError("empty model response")
55	
56	    stripped = text.strip()
57	    fence = re.search(r"```(?:json)?\s*([\s\S]*?)```", stripped, re.IGNORECASE)
58	    if fence:
59	        stripped = fence.group(1).strip()
60	
61	    try:
62	        return json.loads(stripped)
63	    except json.JSONDecodeError:
64	        start = stripped.find("{")
65	        end = stripped.rfind("}")
66	        if start >= 0 and end > start:
67	            return json.loads(stripped[start: end + 1])
68	        start = stripped.find("[")
69	        end = stripped.rfind("]")
70	        if start >= 0 and end > start:
71	            return json.loads(stripped[start: end + 1])
72	        raise

103	    def _call_llm(

2	"""
3	Enhanced YouTube Transcript API Integration
4	Cookie-free, stable transcript extraction using youtube-transcript-api
5	Replaces complex yt-dlp flows with simple, reliable HTTP-based approach
6	
7	Failures are reported as a `reason` code (see REASON_* below) rather than a
8	bare None, because the caller needs to tell three very different things apart:
9	a video that genuinely has no captions, a video we are not allowed to read
10	(private/deleted), and YouTube blocking this IP — which is a property of the
11	run, not of the video, and must not be recorded against 100 episodes as
12	"no transcript".
13	
14	Proxy environment (the documented remedy for an IP block; without one, a
15	blocked run cannot be rescued by retrying from the same address):
16	
17	  YT_WEBSHARE_PROXY_USERNAME / YT_WEBSHARE_PROXY_PASSWORD  Webshare rotating
18	  YT_PROXY_URL (or YT_PROXY_HTTP_URL / YT_PROXY_HTTPS_URL) any HTTP(S) proxy

89	def _classify(exc: Exception) -> str:
90	    """Map a youtube-transcript-api exception to a REASON_* code.
91	
92	    Order matters: IpBlocked subclasses RequestBlocked, and VideoUnplayable
93	    (a private video) is a *sibling* of VideoUnavailable, not a subclass —
94	    which is exactly why private videos used to surface as
95	    "Unexpected error fetching transcript" with a multi-line stderr dump.
96	    """
97	    if isinstance(exc, RequestBlocked):
98	        return REASON_BLOCKED
99	    if isinstance(exc, PoTokenRequired):
100	        return REASON_PO_TOKEN_REQUIRED
101	    if isinstance(exc, VideoUnplayable):
102	        return REASON_PRIVATE
103	    if isinstance(exc, (VideoUnavailable, InvalidVideoId)):
104	        return REASON_UNAVAILABLE
105	    if isinstance(exc, TranscriptsDisabled):
106	        return REASON_TRANSCRIPTS_DISABLED
107	    if isinstance(exc, AgeRestricted):
108	        return REASON_AGE_RESTRICTED
109	    if isinstance(exc, NoTranscriptFound):
110	        return REASON_NO_CAPTIONS
111	    return REASON_ERROR
112	
113	
114	def _short(exc: Exception) -> str:
115	    """First meaningful line of an exception message.
116	
117	    The library's CouldNotRetrieveTranscript messages are ~15 lines of prose
118	    aimed at a human reading a traceback; logging them per video makes a run
119	    log unreadable and buries the one line that identifies the cause.
120	    """
121	    lines = [ln.strip() for ln in str(exc).splitlines() if ln.strip()]
122	    detail = next((ln for ln in lines if not ln.startswith("Could not retrieve")), "")
123	    return f"{type(exc).__name__}: {detail or (lines[0] if lines else 'no detail')}"[:300]

165	def extract_video_id(url: str) -> Optional[str]:
166	    """
167	    Extract YouTube video ID from various URL formats
168	    
169	    Args:
170	        url: YouTube URL in various formats
171	        
172	    Returns:
173	        Video ID string or None if not found
174	    """
175	    try:
176	        p = urlparse(url)
177	        host = (p.hostname or "").lower()
178	        qs = parse_qs(p.query)
179	        
180	        if host not in YOUTUBE_HOSTS:
181	            return None
182	            
183	        # youtu.be format
184	        if "youtu.be" in host:
185	            video_id = p.path.lstrip("/")
186	            return video_id if video_id else None
187	            
188	        # YouTube Shorts format
189	        if p.path.startswith("/shorts/"):
190	            parts = p.path.split("/")
191	            return parts[2] if len(parts) > 2 else None
192	            
193	        # Standard watch URL
194	        if p.path == "/watch":
195	            return qs.get("v", [None])[0]
196	            
197	        # Embed format
198	        if p.path.startswith("/embed/") or p.path.startswith("/v/"):
199	            parts = p.path.split("/")
200	            return parts[2] if len(parts) > 2 else None
201	            
202	        return None
203	        
204	    except Exception as e:
205	        logger.warning(f"Error extracting video ID from {url}: {e}")
206	        return None

255	
256	def _candidates(transcript_list: "TranscriptList", langs: List[str]) -> Iterator[Tuple["Transcript", str]]:
257	    """Yield (transcript, description) in preference order, without fetching.
258	
259	    Fetching is deliberately left to the caller so a failed fetch can be
260	    classified once, in one place, instead of being swallowed by a bare
261	    `except Exception: continue` inside each strategy.
262	    """
263	    seen = set()
264	
265	    def take(transcript, description):
266	        key = (transcript.language_code, transcript.is_generated)
267	        if key in seen:
268	            return None
269	        seen.add(key)
270	        return transcript, description
271	
272	    # 1: manual transcript in a preferred language
273	    for lang in langs:
274	        try:
275	            transcript = transcript_list.find_manually_created_transcript([lang])
276	        except CouldNotRetrieveTranscript:
277	            continue
278	        found = take(transcript, f"manual {transcript.language_code}")
279	        if found:
280	            yield found
281	
282	    # 2: any manual transcript
283	    for transcript in transcript_list:
284	        if not transcript.is_generated:
285	            found = take(transcript, f"manual {transcript.language_code}")
286	            if found:
287	                yield found
288	
289	    # 3: auto-generated in a preferred language
290	    for lang in langs:
291	        try:
292	            transcript = transcript_list.find_generated_transcript([lang])
293	        except CouldNotRetrieveTranscript:
294	            continue
295	        found = take(transcript, f"auto-generated {transcript.language_code}")
296	        if found:
297	            yield found
298	
299	    # 4: translate something into English. Skipped for transcripts that are
300	    # already English — an en->en translate is a wasted round trip that the
301	    # earlier stages would have already returned on success. (It used to run,
302	    # and logged "Using translated transcript from en to en".)
303	    target = (langs[0] if langs else "en").split("-")[0]
304	    for transcript in transcript_list:
305	        if not transcript.is_translatable or transcript.language_code.split("-")[0] == target:
306	            continue
307	        try:
308	            translated = transcript.translate(target)
309	        except CouldNotRetrieveTranscript as e:
310	            logger.debug("Cannot translate %s->%s: %s", transcript.language_code, target, _short(e))
311	            continue
312	        yield translated, f"{transcript.language_code}->{target} translation"
313	
314	
315	def fetch_transcript_with_reason(
316	    video_id: str, languages: Optional[List[str]] = None
317	) -> Tuple[Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]], str]:
318	    """Fetch a transcript, returning (segments, REASON_*).
319	
320	    Preference order: manual in a preferred language, any manual,
321	    auto-generated in a preferred language, then translated into the preferred
322	    language.
323	
324	    A block (RequestBlocked/IpBlocked) aborts immediately instead of walking
325	    the remaining candidates: every one of them would hit the same wall, and
326	    reporting the walk's end as "no suitable transcript" is what previously
327	    turned an IP ban into 55 episodes recorded as having no captions.
328	    """
329	    if not YOUTUBE_TRANSCRIPT_API_AVAILABLE:
330	        logger.warning("youtube-transcript-api not available")
331	        return None, REASON_API_UNAVAILABLE
332	
333	    langs = languages or DEFAULT_EN_LANGS
334	    attempts = max(1, int(os.getenv("YT_TRANSCRIPT_MAX_RETRIES", "2")) + 1)
335	    backoff = float(os.getenv("YT_TRANSCRIPT_BACKOFF", "5"))
336	
337	    for attempt in range(1, attempts + 1):
338	        segments, reason = _fetch_once(video_id, langs)
339	        if reason != REASON_BLOCKED or attempt == attempts:
340	            return segments, reason
341	        # Retrying only helps if egress can change; from a single blocked IP
342	        # it is a guaranteed-failing sleep, so don't pretend otherwise.
343	        if not proxy_configured():
344	            logger.error(
345	                "YouTube blocked this IP for %s and no proxy is configured — not retrying. "
346	                "Set YT_WEBSHARE_PROXY_USERNAME/PASSWORD or YT_PROXY_URL.", video_id)
347	            return None, REASON_BLOCKED
348	        wait = backoff * (2 ** (attempt - 1))
349	        logger.warning("Blocked on %s (attempt %d/%d); retrying in %.0fs via proxy",
350	                       video_id, attempt, attempts, wait)
351	        time.sleep(wait)
352	
353	    return None, REASON_BLOCKED
354	
355	
356	def _fetch_once(video_id: str, langs: List[str]) -> Tuple[Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]], str]:
357	    """One full pass over the candidate transcripts for a video."""
358	    try:
359	        transcript_list = _api().list(video_id)
360	    except CouldNotRetrieveTranscript as e:
361	        reason = _classify(e)
362	        log = logger.error if reason in (REASON_BLOCKED, REASON_ERROR) else logger.info
363	        log("No transcript list for %s (%s) — %s", video_id, reason, _short(e))
364	        return None, reason
365	    except Exception as e:
366	        logger.error("Unexpected error listing transcripts for %s: %s", video_id, _short(e))
367	        return None, REASON_ERROR
368	
369	    last_reason = REASON_NO_CAPTIONS
370	    for transcript, description in _candidates(transcript_list, langs):
371	        try:
372	            segments = transcript.fetch()
373	        except CouldNotRetrieveTranscript as e:
374	            last_reason = _classify(e)
375	            if last_reason == REASON_BLOCKED:
376	                return None, REASON_BLOCKED
377	            logger.warning("Fetch failed for %s (%s): %s", video_id, description, _short(e))
378	            continue
379	        except Exception as e:
380	            last_reason = REASON_ERROR
381	            logger.error("Unexpected error fetching %s (%s): %s", video_id, description, _short(e))
382	            continue
383	        # Logged only after the bytes are in hand. The old code announced
384	        # "Found ... transcript" before fetch(), so a failed fetch produced a
385	        # log that claimed success and a result that said none was found.
386	        logger.info("Fetched %s transcript for %s (%d segments)",
387	                    description, video_id, len(segments))
388	        return segments, REASON_OK
389	
390	    logger.warning("No usable transcript for %s (%s)", video_id, last_reason)
391	    return None, last_reason
392

394	def fetch_transcript_best_effort(video_id: str, languages: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]]:
395	    """Fetch a transcript, discarding the failure reason.
396	
397	    Kept for callers that only care whether a transcript came back; prefer
398	    fetch_transcript_with_reason() so blocks can be told from missing captions.
399	    """
400	    segments, _ = fetch_transcript_with_reason(video_id, languages)
401	    return segments

404	def format_transcript_segments(segments: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> str:
405	    """
406	    Format transcript segments into readable text
407	    
408	    Args:
409	        segments: List of transcript segments with text, start, duration
410	        
411	    Returns:
412	        Formatted transcript text
413	    """
414	    if not segments:
415	        return ""
416	        
417	    formatted_text = []
418	    for segment in segments:
419	        # Handle both dict format and FetchedTranscriptSnippet objects
420	        if hasattr(segment, 'text'):
421	            # FetchedTranscriptSnippet object
422	            text = segment.text.strip()
423	        else:
424	            # Dictionary format
425	            text = segment.get("text", "").strip()
426	            
427	        if text:
428	            formatted_text.append(text)
429	            
430	    return " ".join(formatted_text)

433	def get_metadata_and_transcript_api_first(url: str, languages: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
434	    """
435	    Primary function: Get YouTube metadata and transcript using transcript-api-first approach
436	    
437	    Args:
438	        url: YouTube URL
439	        languages: Preferred language codes
440	        
441	    Returns:
442	        Dictionary with metadata, transcript, and processing information
443	    """
444	    if not YOUTUBE_TRANSCRIPT_API_AVAILABLE:
445	        return {
446	            "ok": False, 
447	            "error": "youtube_transcript_api_not_available",
448	            "fallback_required": True
449	        }
450	        
451	    vid = extract_video_id(url)
452	    if not vid:
453	        return {"ok": False, "error": "no_video_id", "reason": REASON_UNAVAILABLE}
454	
455	    # Transcript first: for a private or deleted video the oEmbed call is a
456	    # guaranteed 403/404, and fetching it first was logging a scary
457	    # "oEmbed fetch failed ... HTTP Error 403" ahead of the real explanation.
458	    transcript_segments, reason = fetch_transcript_with_reason(vid, languages)
459	    transcript_text = format_transcript_segments(transcript_segments or [])
460	    success = bool(transcript_text and transcript_text.strip())
461	
462	    if success or reason not in (REASON_PRIVATE, REASON_UNAVAILABLE):
463	        meta = fetch_oembed_metadata(url)
464	    else:
465	        meta = {"ok": False, "error": f"skipped: video {reason}"}
466	
467	    result = {
468	        "ok": success,
469	        "reason": reason,
470	        "retryable": reason in RETRYABLE_REASONS,
471	        "video_id": vid,
472	        "title": meta.get("title") if meta.get("ok") else f"YouTube Video {vid}",
473	        "uploader": meta.get("author_name") if meta.get("ok") else "",
474	        "thumbnail_url": meta.get("thumbnail_url") if meta.get("ok") else "",
475	        "transcript": transcript_text if success else None,
476	        "transcript_segments": transcript_segments if success else None,
477	        "source": "youtube-transcript-api",
478	        "metadata": {
479	            "video_id": vid,
480	            "url": url,
481	            "type": "youtube_transcript",
482	            "api_source": "youtube-transcript-api",
483	            "oembed_success": meta.get("ok", False),
484	            "transcript_available": success,
485	            "transcript_reason": reason,
486	            "segment_count": len(transcript_segments) if transcript_segments else 0
487	        }
488	    }
489	
490	    if not success:
491	        # A yt-dlp/whisper fallback can rescue missing captions; it cannot
492	        # rescue a blocked IP or a video we have no access to.
493	        result["fallback_required"] = reason not in (REASON_BLOCKED, REASON_PRIVATE, REASON_UNAVAILABLE)
494	        result["error"] = f"no_transcript: {reason}"
495	
496	    return result

# youtube-content skill vs. `dy` (disclosure-rag) pipeline — comparison

**Written:** 2026-08-07 (session timestamp; repo working tree reviewed as of `dy-httpswwwyoutubecomwat` teammate's dirty state, see §7)
**Scope:** Read-only. No ingestion run, no network fetch, no writes to `data/`.

## Executive summary

**Recommendation: (c) keep them separate, with a stated boundary.** The global `youtube-content` skill (`/Users/liamellis/skills/media/youtube-content/`) is a thin, stateless wrapper around `youtube-transcript-api` for single-video, throwaway conversational transforms (chapters/summary/thread/blog) — it has no retry logic, no quality gate, no persistence, and no concept of "safe to embed." The repo's `dy` pipeline (`apps/disclosure-rag/scripts/playlist_ingestion.py` + `lib/transcript_fidelity.py` + `processing/rag_prompt_pipeline.py`) is the only one of the two with fidelity scoring, quarantine, an Evidence/Inference separation (ADR-0001), checkpointed state, and provenance reporting — everything this project's epistemic-honesty constraint requires before content reaches the RAG corpus. They are not redundant: the skill's output-format transforms (chapters/threads/blogs) are a genuinely distinct capability `dy` doesn't have in code, but that capability is generative paraphrase and must never be treated as ingestible Evidence. Two small, low-cost items are worth porting into `dy` (a `/live/` URL-parsing branch; possibly a lightweight non-ingesting "peek" command); everything else should stay on its own side of the line. No hard dependency conflict exists between the two (both use `youtube-transcript-api` 1.x, different patch versions, fully isolated environments).

---

## 1. Capability matrix

| Capability | Skill | `dy` | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Transcript fetch | `fetch_transcript.py:63-67`, single `YouTubeTranscriptApi().fetch()` call | `lib/youtube_transcript_enhanced.py:356-391` (`_fetch_once`), full candidate-tier search | both (dy superset) |
| URL/ID format handling | `fetch_transcript.py:26-37` regex incl. `live/` | `lib/youtube_transcript_enhanced.py:165-206` `extract_video_id`, host-allowlist based; **no `/live/` branch** | both, skill has one thing dy lacks |
| Language selection + fallback | `fetch_transcript.py:64-67`, one-shot `languages=[...]`; fallback is a *manual agent step* per `SKILL.md:75` | `lib/youtube_transcript_enhanced.py:256-312` `_candidates()`: manual-preferred → any-manual → auto-generated-preferred → translate-to-target, all in one call | both (dy substantially deeper) |
| Timestamps | `fetch_transcript.py:40-47,103-105`, `--timestamps` produces a persisted timestamped-text output | segment `start`/`duration` used internally for fidelity scoring (`lib/transcript_fidelity.py:84-99`) but **dropped** from the saved artifact — `scripts/playlist_ingestion.py:255-259` writes only title+url+cleaned prose, no per-line timestamps | both, but only skill *persists* a timestamped artifact |
| Playlist/channel/batch handling | none | `scripts/playlist_ingestion.py:87-156` `enumerate_playlist()`, yt-dlp flat extraction + pytube fallback | dy-only |
| Rate limiting & retry | none | proxy-aware exponential backoff (`lib/youtube_transcript_enhanced.py:334-352`) + run-level circuit breaker (`scripts/playlist_ingestion.py:426-441`, `BLOCKED_ABORT_THRESHOLD`) | dy-only |
| Caching / idempotency | none — every call re-fetches | `state.json` checkpoint, skip `DONE_STATUSES` (`scripts/playlist_ingestion.py:57,161-195,401-406`), `--force` override | dy-only |
| No transcript / disabled | string-match on `"disabled"`/`"no transcript"` in exception text (`fetch_transcript.py:94-97`) | `REASON_TRANSCRIPTS_DISABLED`, `REASON_NO_CAPTIONS` via typed exception classification (`lib/youtube_transcript_enhanced.py:67-111`) | both, dy structured / skill string-sniffed |
| Members-only / private / deleted | undistinguished — falls into the generic error branch | `REASON_PRIVATE` (`VideoUnplayable`), `REASON_UNAVAILABLE` (`VideoUnavailable`/`InvalidVideoId`), marked **terminal** (`youtube_transcript_enhanced.py:83-86,101-104`) | dy-only structured handling |
| Age-gated | undistinguished | `REASON_AGE_RESTRICTED` via `AgeRestricted` exception (`lib/youtube_transcript_enhanced.py:107-108`) | dy-only |
| Region-blocked | undistinguished | not named as its own `REASON_*`; likely folds into `REASON_ERROR` — **UNVERIFIED**, did not trace whether `youtube-transcript-api` 1.2.x raises a distinct region-block exception | neither confirmed |
| IP-blocked (rate limit) | undistinguished, would surface as opaque error JSON | `REASON_BLOCKED` (`RequestBlocked`/`IpBlocked`), retryable only with a configured proxy, run-level abort after 3 consecutive blocks (`lib/youtube_transcript_enhanced.py:97-98,343-353`; `scripts/playlist_ingestion.py:60-72,426-441`) | dy-only |
| Auto-generated-only captions | handled implicitly (single `.fetch()` returns whatever's available) | handled explicitly as candidate tier 3 (`_candidates()` line 289-297), not treated as an error | both |
| Output formats | JSON / plain text / timestamped text (`fetch_transcript.py:107-121`); chapters/summary/thread/blog/quotes are agent-driven transforms per `SKILL.md:42-61` + `references/output-formats.md` | cleaned plain-text transcript file only (`scripts/playlist_ingestion.py:255-259`) | skill-only for reader-facing transforms |
| Downstream processing (chunk/embed/NER/index) | none | 5-stage registry pipeline: classification → content_analysis → rag_ingestion (chunking) → NER → validation (`processing/rag_prompt_pipeline.py:151-330`), feeds OpenAI vector store / Xata / CocoIndex / Mem0 | dy-only |
| Provenance / metadata capture | none — JSON output has only `video_id`/`segment_count`/`duration`/`full_text` | per-episode `reports/<id>.fidelity.json` (score, verdict, subscores, word/coverage/wpm/gap/artifact/repetition — verified sample `2ttdlCa5ZCI.fidelity.json`), `state.json` per-video doc_id/status/fidelity/timestamps | dy-only |
| Reporting | none | per-run markdown summary (`scripts/playlist_ingestion.py:325-346`, verified sample `run-20260807-084928.md`: status counts + per-episode table) | dy-only |

## 2. Overlap and redundancy

The only genuine overlap is the raw fetch step, and even there it's a subset relationship, not duplication:

- Skill: `scripts/fetch_transcript.py:63-67` — `YouTubeTranscriptApi().fetch(video_id, languages=languages)`, one call, first match, done.
- `dy`: `lib/youtube_transcript_enhanced.py:356-391` `_fetch_once()` — `.list(video_id)` then walks `_candidates()`'s four-tier preference order, catching and classifying exceptions per candidate rather than per call.

Both depend on the same library, `youtube-transcript-api`, both on the 1.x line:
- `apps/disclosure-rag/requirements.txt:39` pins `youtube-transcript-api>=1.2  # 1.x exception classes + proxies module are required` — this constraint was added in the currently-uncommitted diff (`git diff apps/disclosure-rag/requirements.txt` shows the old line was an unpinned `youtube-transcript-api`). Installed in the repo `.venv`: **1.2.2**.
- The global skill's environment (managed via `uv`, no `pyproject.toml` found anywhere under `/Users/liamellis/skills/`) has **1.2.4** installed (`uv pip list`).

No conflict: same major version, both post-1.0 (needed for the exception classes and `proxies` module `dy` imports at `lib/youtube_transcript_enhanced.py:34-48`), fully separate environments (see §6).

`rag_prompt_pipeline.py`'s chunking stage does **not** overlap with the skill's chapters/summary/thread/blog transforms, despite both being "take transcript, produce structured text." The pipeline's own docstring draws the line: *"Chunk bodies remain Evidence-only (ADR-0001): never embed agent Inference"* (`processing/rag_prompt_pipeline.py:9-10`). Its chunks are RAG-indexing units, not reader content. The skill's transforms are explicitly interpretive/summarizing. These are different jobs that happen to both start from a transcript.

## 3. What the skill has that `dy` lacks — worth adopting

1. **`/live/` URL parsing.** `scripts/fetch_transcript.py:30` includes a `live/` branch in its video-ID regex. `dy`'s `extract_video_id` (`lib/youtube_transcript_enhanced.py:165-206`) has an explicit if/elif chain for `youtu.be`, `/shorts/`, `/watch`, `/embed/` and `/v/` but **no `/live/` case** — a livestream URL passed to `dy` would fall through to `return None`. Concrete port: add `elif p.path.startswith("/live/"): return p.path.split("/")[2] if ... else None` mirroring the shorts branch at lines 189-191. Trivial, a few lines.

2. **Content-transformation formats** (chapters, summary, chapter-summaries, Twitter thread, blog post, quotes — `SKILL.md:42-61`, `references/output-formats.md`). Confirmed this does *not* overlap with `rag_ingestion`'s chunking (see §2) — it's a genuinely distinct, currently-absent capability in `dy`. Porting cost is low in principle (it's prompt-engineering/agent-workflow, not a script dependency), but see §4/§6: this output is generative paraphrase and must not be treated as embeddable Evidence if ported.

3. **Lightweight one-shot text output** (`--text-only`, `--timestamps` on `fetch_transcript.py`) for a quick "just show me the transcript" lookup outside the full ingestion pipeline. `dy` has no equivalent non-ingesting single-video peek command in the files reviewed — **UNVERIFIED** whether `main.py`'s `--no-kb` flag (referenced in `disclosure-rag-processor/SKILL.md:36,94-95`) provides this; `main.py` itself was not read in this session, so I can't confirm whether `--no-kb` still runs the full `rag_prompt_pipeline` (LLM calls) or is truly lightweight.

## 4. What `dy` has that the skill lacks

This is where the epistemic-honesty gap is concrete, not abstract:

- **Fidelity scoring.** `lib/transcript_fidelity.py:165-254` `review_transcript()` — weighted composite (coverage .30, density .20, gaps .15, artifacts .15, repetition .20), verdicts `pass`(≥0.7)/`review`(0.45-0.7)/`fail`(<0.45). The skill has **zero** quality signal: it would hand a 40%-coverage, artifact-heavy auto-caption transcript straight into a "blog post" transform with no warning beyond a subjective "re-read for coherence" step (`SKILL.md:69`).
- **Quarantine gate.** Fidelity `fail` or below `--min-fidelity` → `status="quarantined"`, transcript and report kept on disk but **not ingested** (`scripts/playlist_ingestion.py:274-278`; `references/playlist-ingestion.md:41-43`).
- **Evidence/Inference separation (ADR-0001).** `processing/rag_prompt_pipeline.py:9-10` docstring is explicit; enforced at `lines 288-301` where chunks a validation pass marks `safe_for_rag_index: False` are excluded from `embeddable_texts`. This is exactly the "invent/paraphrase/lossily summarize into the corpus" guard the task brief calls a hard constraint — and it's precisely what the skill's chapters/summary/thread/blog output would violate if fed into the KB directly, since those formats are inherently paraphrase with no sourcing discipline documented anywhere in `SKILL.md`.
- **Full provenance chain.** `doc_id`, `fidelity`, `rag_status`, timestamps recorded per video in `state.json` (`scripts/playlist_ingestion.py:184-194`); per-run markdown report (`scripts/playlist_ingestion.py:325-346`). The skill produces stdout only — nothing survives the conversation.

## 5. Recommendation

**(c) Keep them separate, with a stated boundary:**

- The global `youtube-content` skill is for **disposable, single-video, out-of-corpus** conversational work — "summarize this video for me right now," not "add this to the knowledge base."
- `dy` (via `scripts/playlist_ingestion.py` / `main.py`) remains the **only** path allowed to write into the corpus, because it's the only one with fidelity gating, quarantine, and the Evidence/Inference split.
- Porting worth doing, low cost: the `/live/` URL branch (§3.1, a few lines). Optional: a lightweight non-ingesting peek command if `main.py --no-kb` doesn't already serve that role (§3.3, UNVERIFIED — would need to read `main.py` to size this).
- Not worth porting: the output-format transforms as a `dy` feature, because doing so would put generative-paraphrase code inside the pipeline that's supposed to enforce Evidence-only chunking. If a user wants both a corpus entry *and* a reader-facing summary of the same video, that should be two separate operations, not one pipeline doing both.
- Retire nothing — the skill is not subsumed; it does a job `dy` deliberately doesn't do.

## 6. Risks / conflicts

- **Dependency version:** repo `.venv` has `youtube-transcript-api==1.2.2` (pinned `>=1.2` in `requirements.txt:39`, that pin itself added in the currently-uncommitted diff); the skill's `uv`-managed environment has `1.2.4`. def extract_video_id(url: str) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Extract YouTube video ID from various URL formats
    
    Args:
        url: YouTube URL in various formats
        
    Returns:
        Video ID string or None if not found
    """
    try:
        p = urlparse(url)
        host = (p.hostname or "").lower()
        qs = parse_qs(p.query)
        
        if host not in YOUTUBE_HOSTS:
            return None
            
        # youtu.be format
        if "youtu.be" in host:
            video_id = p.path.lstrip("/")
            return video_id if video_id else None
            
        # YouTube Shorts format
        if p.path.startswith("/shorts/"):
            parts = p.path.split("/")
            return parts[2] if len(parts) > 2 else None
            
        # Standard watch URL
        if p.path == "/watch":
            return qs.get("v", [None])[0]
            
        # Embed format
        if p.path.startswith("/embed/") or p.path.startswith("/v/"):
            parts = p.path.split("/")
            return parts[2] if len(parts) > 2 else None
            
        return None
        
    except Exception as e:
        logger.warning(f"Error extracting video ID from {url}: {e}")
        return None

154	def is_youtube_url(url: str) -> bool:
155	    """Check if URL's hostname is a YouTube domain (not a substring match).
156	
157	    A substring check (`'youtube.com' in url`) accepts hostile URLs like
158	    `https://evil.com/?x=youtube.com/watch` - parse the hostname instead.
159	    """
160	    try:
161	        hostname = (urlparse(url).hostname or "").lower()
162	    except ValueError:
163	        return False
164	    if hostname.startswith("www."):
165	        hostname = hostname[4:]
166	    return hostname in _YOUTUBE_HOSTNAMES or hostname.endswith(".youtube.com")
167

205	def _detail(value: Any, limit: int = 200) -> str:
206	    """Coerce any value into a short, printable string.
207	
208	    Prevents raw API-response objects (e.g. queue_result['qstash_response'])
209	    from leaking into printed output the way `data['file_paths']` values did
210	    (T-045 H7's "Files Created" bug) - every stage detail must be a plain
211	    string here, not whatever shape an upstream dict happened to contain.
212	    """
213	    if value is None:
214	        return ""
215	    text = value if isinstance(value, str) else str(value)
216	    return text if len(text) <= limit else text[:limit - 1] + "…"
217
